relationships.detail: The arrogant esper picks a fight with Mob to prove his superiority, loses, and becomes one of Mob's most dependable friends.

relationships.name: Dimple
relationships.detail: After Mob beats him, the scheming spirit tags along; later he tries to become a god through the Divine Tree, and Mob talks him down as a friend.

relationships.name: Tsubomi Takane
relationships.detail: Mob trains for the school marathon hoping to confess to her; when he finally does, she kindly turns him down.

relationships.name: Toichiro Suzuki
relationships.detail: Claw's founder can store and hand out psychic energy; their final battle above Seasoning City ends with Mob absorbing his runaway power.

fights.title: Mob vs. Teru
fights.summary: Mob refuses to use his powers on a person while Teru wrecks everything around them, until Teru chokes him unconscious and Mob's ???% state erupts, flattening the school and ending the fight.

fights.title: Storming the Seventh Division
fights.summary: Cornered by Claw's top espers, Mob unknowingly pours his power into Reigen, who then faces the Scars in his place.

fights.title: Trapped in Mogami's world
fights.summary: The spirit Keiji Mogami pulls Mob into an illusory life where he is bullied without end, testing whether he will use his powers to hurt people.

fights.title: Mob vs. Toichiro Suzuki
fights.summary: Above Seasoning City, Mob fights Claw's leader on equal terms, then absorbs and redirects his overloaded power to prevent a huge explosion.

fights.title: Inside the Divine Tree
fights.summary: Mob reaches 100% but chooses not to fight, and his heart-to-heart persuades Dimple to give up godhood.

keyEpisodes.why: Debut: Mob exorcises spirits for Reigen with almost no effort.
His duel with Teru shows how dangerous his bottled-up feelings can be.
Mob realises Reigen has been using him and parts ways with his master.
The end of the Claw war and the birth of the Divine Tree.
Finale: Mob accepts all of himself, confesses to Tsubomi and grows up.

strength.rank: Immensely powerful esper
strength.summary: Mob's powers are tied to his suppressed emotions, which build toward 100% before exploding outward. His unconscious ???% state wrecks a school and ends Teru's challenge, and in season 2 he stops Claw's leader Toichiro Suzuki from blowing up the city by taking the energy into himself.

qualities.detail: At Doll training school she ghostwrites a classmate's letter as a dry list of facts, and the instructor rejects it for carrying none of the feelings a letter is supposed to convey.
She has spent her life following commands, so when she asks Hodgins to let her join the ghostwriting department, he is struck that it is the first thing she has chosen for herself.
She becomes an Auto Memory Doll for one reason: to find out what Gilbert meant by 'I love you', the last words he said to her.
She clings to Gilbert's emerald brooch, and when Hodgins returns it to her she is openly overjoyed, a rare show of emotion that says how much he means to her.
Early on, technically flawless but blind to feelings, she drafts a love letter that leaves the client and its recipient both furious.

violet-evergarden.backstory: Violet remembers nothing of her parents or origins. As a young girl she fell into the hands of Dietfried Bougainvillea, a navy officer, who saw her as a tool of war and handed her to his younger brother, Major Gilbert Bougainvillea of the Leidenschaftlich Army. Gilbert hoped to raise her as an ordinary girl, but his superiors sent her to the front as a child soldier because of her fighting skill. He gave her the name Violet, taught her to read and write, and bought her an emerald brooch that reminded her of his eyes. In the war's final assault Gilbert was badly wounded, and Violet lost both arms trying to carry him out. Before the enemy bombed the building, he told her he loved her, words she could not understand. She was fitted with prosthetic arms and left waiting for orders from a man everyone else believed dead.

journey.summary: With the war over, Hodgins brings Violet to Leiden and to his CH Postal Company. She asks to become an Auto Memory Doll, struggles with clients because she can't read emotions, and finally graduates from Doll school by writing a short, honest letter from her friend Luculia to her troubled brother.

Job by job she learns how people hide what they feel: she helps Iris make amends with her family, gets a prince and princess to write their own love letters, and helps the grieving playwright Oscar finish a story for his late daughter.

Dietfried confirms that Gilbert is presumed dead, and Violet, who had refused to believe it, finds his grave. Flashbacks show her years at his side and the battle that cost her arms, and for a while she is so consumed by guilt that she stops working.

Back at work, she writes fifty birthday letters for a dying mother to leave her young daughter Anne, and then reaches a dying soldier, Aidan, in time to write his last letters and comfort him at the end, weeping afterward that she couldn't bring him home.

journey.stage: Peace treaty and the Air Show (episodes 12-13)
journey.summary: Helping protect a peace envoy on his way to sign the treaty, she shields Dietfried from a grenade and tells him that Gilbert's final command to her was to go on living. She then writes her own letter to Gilbert for the revived Air Show, saying she now understands 'I love you' and will keep living.

Hodgins discovers that Gilbert is alive, teaching on the remote island of Ecarte. Gilbert at first refuses to see her out of guilt, but after reading her farewell letter he runs after her ship. They reunite, and Violet leaves the CH Postal Company to make a life with him on the island.

lessons.lesson: Feelings are learned, not switched on.
lessons.why: Violet arrives unable to read any emotion, and it is through clients like Iris, Oscar and Ann that she slowly learns what people mean beneath their words.

lessons.lesson: The past can't be undone, but neither can the good you do now.
lessons.why: When Violet asks whether someone like her should keep living, Hodgins points out that her kind acts as a Doll are as permanent as her actions in the war.

lessons.lesson: Saying what you feel takes courage.
lessons.why: Unable to write her own letter to Gilbert, Violet realises how much courage his confession must have taken, and she only finds her own words in the letter she writes for the Air Show.

relationships.name: Gilbert Bougainvillea
relationships.detail: Gilbert named Violet, taught her to read and write, and told her 'I love you' in their last moments on the battlefield; learning what those words mean is why she becomes a Doll.

relationships.name: Claudia Hodgins
relationships.detail: Gilbert's old friend collects Violet from the hospital, hires her at his CH Postal Company and, as Gilbert asked, looks after her.

relationships.name: Dietfried Bougainvillea
relationships.detail: Dietfried handed the young Violet to Gilbert's command as a child soldier and later blames her for Gilbert's loss, until she risks her arms to save him on the peace-treaty train.

relationships.name: Cattleya Baudelaire
relationships.detail: The CH Postal Company's veteran Auto Memory Doll oversees Violet's first steps in ghostwriting.

relationships.name: Benedict Blue
relationships.detail: The company's postman ends up beside Violet on the hijacked train and helps her remove the bombs from the bridge.

relationships.name: Luculia Marlborough
relationships.detail: Violet's classmate at the school where Dolls are trained; Violet later ghostwrites a letter for Luculia's brother.

fights.title: Asking to become a Doll
fights.summary: Watching Dolls write a love letter reminds Violet of Gilbert's last words, and for the first time she asks for something on her own: a place in the ghostwriting department.

fights.title: The last battle with Gilbert
fights.summary: In flashback, Violet loses both arms trying to drag the wounded Gilbert to safety, and he tells her he loves her before pushing her clear.

fights.title: Fifty birthdays of letters
fights.summary: Hired by a dying mother, Violet writes letters to be delivered to her young daughter Anne every birthday for the next fifty years.

fights.title: Defending the peace-treaty train
fights.summary: Violet protects Dietfried from anti-peace rebels and tears out the bombs on the bridge, losing both prosthetic arms.

fights.title: Journey to Ecarte
fights.summary: A letter in Gilbert's handwriting leads Violet and Hodgins to a remote island, where they find him alive.

keyEpisodes.why: Debut: Violet leaves the army and joins the CH Postal Company.
Violet is told Gilbert is presumed dead and refuses to believe it.
The full story of Gilbert's last words, and Violet's decision to keep living.
Series finale: the peace treaty is signed and Violet writes her own letter to Gilbert.
The sequel film resolves Violet's story with Gilbert.

strength.rank: Former child soldier with remarkable combat skill
strength.summary: Before she became an Auto Memory Doll, Violet's fighting ability made her central to winning many key battles in Gilbert's unit. Even with prosthetic arms and a refusal to kill, she shields Dietfried from a rifle grenade on the peace-treaty train and gives up both mechanical arms to stop the attack.

qualities.detail: Starved of recognition, he plays pranks for attention; his first scene has him painting graffiti on the stone faces of the Hokage monument.
He tells anyone who will listen that he will become Hokage, because he believes that is how the village will finally have to acknowledge him.
After failing the academy exam on a botched clone technique, he masters the far harder Multi-Shadow Clone Jutsu in a single night.
When Zabuza traps Kakashi in the Land of Waves and Kakashi orders the team to run, Naruto stays and, with Sasuke, frees their teacher.
Having grown up shunned, he recognises the same loneliness in others, from the grieving boy Inari to the feared Sand ninja Gaara.

naruto-uzumaki.backstory: Naruto was born in Konoha on the night the Nine-Tailed Fox, Kurama, attacked the village. His father, Minato Namikaze, the Fourth Hokage, sealed the fox inside the newborn, and both Minato and Naruto's mother, Kushina Uzumaki, died that night. Naruto grew up an orphan who didn't know who his parents were. The villagers were forbidden to mention the fox, yet they treated the boy who carried it with fear and contempt, and being seen with him was taboo. Lonely and ignored, Naruto turned into a prankster and a class clown, and set his heart on becoming Hokage so that everyone would have to respect him. His academy teacher, Iruka Umino, was one of the few adults who saw past the fox, and he became something close to a father figure.

journey.summary: Tricked by the teacher Mizuki into stealing a secret scroll, Naruto learns that the Nine-Tails is sealed inside him, but Iruka stands up for him. He then joins Team 7 under Kakashi, alongside his rival Sasuke and his crush Sakura.

journey.stage: Land of Waves and the Chunin Exams
journey.summary: On his first real mission he discovers what being a ninja costs when Haku dies protecting Zabuza. During the Chunin Exams he trains with Jiraiya, learns to summon toads, and during the invasion of the village he defeats Gaara and shows him there is another way to live.

journey.stage: Search for Tsunade and Sasuke Recovery Mission
journey.summary: He learns the Rasengan while travelling with Jiraiya to bring back Tsunade as Hokage. When Sasuke leaves to join Orochimaru, Naruto chases him to the Valley of the End and loses, then sets off to train under Jiraiya, spending some two and a half years away, rather than give up on his friend.

journey.stage: Kazekage Rescue and the hunt for Sasuke (Shippuden)
journey.summary: Back home, he helps rescue Gaara from Akatsuki and creates the Wind Release: Rasenshuriken, which turns the tide against Kakuzu, while the Nine-Tails' chakra threatens to take him over more and more.

After Jiraiya's death, Naruto masters sage techniques and returns to find his village in ruins. In the fight he nearly gives in to the fox, but meets the memory of his father sealed inside him, regains control, defeats Pain, and talks Nagato into giving up his plan, which saves the village.

With help from his mother's imprint in the seal, Naruto takes control of the Nine-Tails' power and later makes peace with Kurama. He and Sasuke stand together against Obito, Madara and Kaguya, then fight one last time at the Valley of the End; both lose an arm, and they finally make peace.

In the epilogue he is married to Hinata, with two children, and serves as the Seventh Hokage. In the sequel Boruto he loses Kurama in the battle with Isshiki and is later sealed away by Kawaki, but he is not dead.

lessons.lesson: Being seen by even one person can change a life.
lessons.why: Iruka's choice to stand up for Naruto against Mizuki gives him the acceptance the rest of the village refused, and he passes the same recognition on to Gaara and Nagato.

lessons.lesson: Refusing to give up on someone is a choice you keep making.
lessons.why: Naruto loses to Sasuke at the Valley of the End as a boy, trains for years, and keeps chasing him until they finally reconcile after their last fight.

lessons.lesson: Ending a cycle of hatred takes understanding, not just winning.
lessons.why: After defeating Pain, Naruto doesn't kill Nagato; he talks to him as a fellow student of Jiraiya, and that conversation is what saves the village.

relationships.name: Sasuke Uchiha
relationships.detail: Naruto calls the last Uchiha a brother and chases him for years after Sasuke defects; their rivalry is settled only in a final battle back at the valley where Sasuke first left him behind.

relationships.name: Sakura Haruno
relationships.detail: Naruto spends much of Part I trying, and failing, to win over his Team 7 teammate, who comes to rely on him as a comrade.

relationships.name: Jiraiya

relationships.name: Kurama (Nine-Tails)
relationships.detail: The fox sealed in Naruto at birth is the reason the village shunned him; during the war Naruto befriends it and they combine their chakra.

relationships.name: Hinata Hyuga
relationships.detail: Hinata confesses her love while shielding Naruto from Pain, and the two marry after the war.

relationships.name: Gaara

fights.title: Naruto vs. Neji
fights.summary: In the Chūnin Exam finals, Naruto taps the Nine-Tails' chakra and beats Neji with a shadow clone decoy, then tells him to stop blaming fate.

fights.title: Naruto vs. Gaara
fights.summary: With Gamabunta holding Shukaku down, Naruto wakes Gaara and smashes the sand beast apart, ending their battle.

fights.title: Valley of the End
fights.summary: Naruto's Rasengan and Sasuke's Chidori collide one last time, and Sasuke walks away to join Orochimaru.

fights.title: Naruto vs. Pain
fights.summary: After Sage Mode and a near-loss to the Nine-Tails' rage, Naruto destroys the last of Pain's bodies with a Rasengan and goes to face Nagato.

fights.title: Partnering with Kurama
fights.summary: Naruto declares the Nine-Tails his friend, they merge their chakra, and his new Tailed Beast Mode turns the battle against the captured tailed beasts.

fights.title: The final battle with Sasuke
fights.summary: Their Rasenshuriken and Indra's Arrow tear the Valley of the End apart, and the drained pair trade punches until one last Rasengan meets one last Chidori.

Naruto comes home to the Leaf after more than two years away training under Jiraiya.
The village that once shunned him celebrates him as its hero after Pain's attack.
The war ends and the two rivals undo the Infinite Tsukuyomi together.
Final episode: Naruto and Hinata's wedding.

strength.rank: Host of the Nine-Tails and 'Hero of the Hidden Leaf'
strength.summary: Naruto's mass Shadow Clones and Rasengan grow into Sage Mode, which he uses to defeat all six Paths of Pain. Once he befriends Kurama he gains a Tailed Beast Mode strong enough to take on several tailed beasts at once, and he and Sasuke seal away Kaguya at the end of the war.

qualities.detail: When Yuji swallows Sukuna's finger and stays in control, Megumi still judges him a threat and gets ready to exorcise him, as protocol demands.
He later admits he chose to spare Yuji because he wants to save people who deserve saving, rules or not, and says he doesn't regret it.
When a special-grade curse ambushes the first-years at the detention center, Megumi gets Nobara out while Yuji holds the curse off.
He keeps people at a distance, and his friendship with the loud Yuji and the brash Nobara starts out as a reluctant one.
His stepsister Tsumiki, left in a coma by a curse, is the reason he wants to save people at all.

jujutsu-kaisen-megumi-fushiguro.backstory: Megumi is the son of Toji Fushiguro, a man born into the powerful Zen'in clan without cursed energy, who left the clan and took the name Fushiguro when he married. Megumi's parents were out of the picture early, and he grew up with his stepsister Tsumiki, whose plain goodness he looked up to even as he argued with her. Toji arranged to sell his son to the Zen'in clan, believing it would give the boy a better future, and then died fighting Satoru Gojo; Megumi had inherited the clan's prized Ten Shadows Technique. A few years later Gojo tracked six-year-old Megumi down and took him under his wing to keep him out of the Zen'in clan's hands. When Tsumiki fell into a coma caused by a curse, Megumi's reason to become a sorcerer took shape, and he enrolled at Tokyo Jujutsu High under Gojo.

journey.summary: Sent to retrieve one of Sukuna's fingers from a high school, Megumi ends up fighting curses beside Yuji, who swallows the finger to save them both. He is ready to exorcise Yuji until Gojo steps in and has Yuji trained instead, and the two become classmates with Nobara.

Against a special-grade curse he gets Nobara to safety, then faces Sukuna in Yuji's body and loses badly, though Sukuna takes a strange interest in him. Watching Yuji apparently die, he explains why he chose to save him.
Paired against Kyoto's Noritoshi Kamo, he ends up fighting the special-grade curse Hanami alongside his rival and is badly hurt.
Hunting a curse that threatens his comatose sister, Megumi is pushed to his limit, recalls Gojo's advice, and manages his first-ever Domain Expansion, which he calls Chimera Shadow Garden.

He helps break the veils around Shibuya, then is attacked by his resurrected father, Toji, who recognises him and ends his own possession, glad Megumi turned away from the Zen'in name. Nearly killed by a curse user moments later, Megumi summons the untamed Mahoraga to take them both down, and Sukuna steps in to save him.

With Tsumiki's body taken over by the ancient sorcerer Yorozu and forced into the Culling Game, Megumi enters the game with Yuji to get her out, and along the way becomes head of the Zen'in clan. Sukuna then seizes Megumi's body and uses it to kill Yorozu in Tsumiki's body, plunging Megumi into despair.

Trapped inside his own body while Sukuna fights the strongest sorcerers, Megumi has all but given up until Yuji forces Sukuna out and frees him. He survives to the end of the manga (chapter 271, 2024); the anime has not reached these chapters.

lessons.lesson: Doing what's right sometimes means breaking the rules.
lessons.why: Megumi is supposed to exorcise Yuji, but he decides Yuji is worth saving and stands by that choice even after it costs him.

lessons.lesson: You may be stronger than you think when you stop holding back.
lessons.why: Only when he is cornered and recalls Gojo's advice does Megumi manage his first Domain Expansion.

lessons.lesson: Where you come from doesn't decide who you are.
lessons.why: Born a Zen'in and nearly sold to them, Megumi chooses Gojo's path instead, and even his father's resurrected body recognises that choice before Toji ends his own life.

relationships.name: Satoru Gojo
relationships.detail: Gojo has looked out for Megumi since he was six and teaches him at Jujutsu High; Gojo's advice helps Megumi unlock his Domain Expansion.

relationships.name: Yuji Itadori
relationships.detail: Megumi meets Yuji while hunting for Sukuna's finger and chooses to spare him after Yuji becomes Sukuna's vessel, a decision he never regrets.

relationships.name: Nobara Kugisaki
relationships.detail: The third member of the Tokyo first-years, Nobara joins Megumi and Yuji on most of their missions.

relationships.name: Tsumiki Fushiguro
relationships.detail: Seeing Tsumiki fall into a coma because of a curse is what drives Megumi to save people, and a curse threatening her pushes him into his first Domain Expansion.

relationships.name: Sukuna
relationships.detail: Sukuna beats Megumi early on but takes a keen interest in his potential, later stepping in to destroy Mahoraga and keep him alive in Shibuya.

relationships.name: Toji Fushiguro
relationships.detail: Resurrected in Shibuya, Toji attacks Megumi without knowing him; on learning his son kept the name Fushiguro, Toji ends the possession by killing himself.

fights.title: Megumi vs. Sukuna
fights.summary: Sukuna takes Yuji's body hostage and tears out his heart; Megumi faces him alone and loses, but catches the curse's interest.

fights.title: Chimera Shadow Garden
fights.summary: Left alone against a special-grade curse, Megumi stops holding back and forms a Domain of his own to exorcise it.

fights.title: Megumi vs. Toji
fights.summary: In Shibuya, Megumi is overwhelmed by a revived sorcerer killer who turns out to be his own father.

fights.title: Summoning Mahoraga
fights.summary: Close to death, Megumi performs the ritual to call Mahoraga, forcing Sukuna to take over Yuji's body and destroy it with Malevolent Shrine.

fights.title: Megumi vs. Reggie Star
fights.summary: In the Culling Game's Tokyo Colony No. 1, Megumi drops Reggie into a pool to ruin his receipts and finishes him with his Divine Dog.

His first Domain Expansion and memories of Tsumiki.
Megumi's encounter with his father in Shibuya.
The Zen'in clan learns that Megumi, not Naoya, is set to inherit as clan head.
Megumi wins his first Culling Game battle, then collapses before he can finish off Remi.

ages.when: Start of the series (first-year at Jujutsu High)

strength.rank: Ten Shadows user and future Zen'in clan heir
strength.summary: Megumi's Ten Shadows Technique summons shikigami from shadows, though he must defeat each one in battle before he can control it. Against a special-grade curse he opens his Domain, Chimera Shadow Garden, for the very first time, and in Shibuya he calls up Mahoraga, a shikigami no previous user had ever tamed.

qualities.detail: In his first months at U.A. he keeps to himself and makes little effort to get to know his classmates.
He refuses to use the fire side of his Quirk because it came from his father, and fights with ice alone even against the strongest opponents.
Before the Sports Festival he walks up to Izuku and tells him plainly that he intends to beat him.
When Izuku sends him a cryptic message from Hosu City, Todoroki goes straight to help and arrives just in time to fight the Hero Killer Stain beside him.
In the end-of-term exam, he backs Momo Yaoyorozu's plan against Aizawa and tells her he voted for her as class president.

shouto-todoroki.backstory: The pro hero Endeavor and his wife, Rei, had four children, and Shoto is the last of them. Their marriage was a 'Quirk marriage': Endeavor chose Rei to produce a child whose combined fire and ice powers could surpass All Might, and Shoto was the only child who turned out the way he wanted. From then on Endeavor put the small boy through brutal training and kept him apart from his brothers and sister. Rei, worn down by her husband's abuse, broke one day and poured boiling water over the left half of her son's face because it reminded her of Endeavor, leaving the scar around his eye; she was then sent to a hospital. Around the same time his eldest brother, Toya, was believed to have died in a fire. Shoto grew up hating his father and swearing that he would become a hero using only his mother's ice.

journey.summary: Todoroki tears through the early events and tells Izuku about the Quirk marriage that made him. In their match Izuku goads him into unleashing his fire at full strength, but in the final he lets his flames die and loses to Bakugo. Afterwards he goes to see his mother for the first time in years.

Answering Izuku's message, he fights Stain with Izuku and Ida, using fire and ice together. Endeavor takes official credit for the arrest so the students escape punishment for fighting without a hero license.

A grudge against Endeavor makes Shiketsu's Inasa Yoarashi clash with Todoroki mid-exam, and their feud derails the rescue scenario; both fail the license test, a hard lesson about letting his father's shadow get in the way.

Fighting alongside Izuku, Bakugo and Endeavor against Shigaraki, he then watches the villain Dabi publicly reveal that he is Toya, his brother who supposedly died. Todoroki is overpowered by Dabi, and after he recovers he resolves that stopping his brother is his job.

Facing Dabi again, he unveils Flashfire Fist: Phosphor, a move that merges his hot and cold sides, and knocks his brother down. When Dabi rises again and is about to explode, Todoroki rides Ida's engine-powered ice jet to the scene and smothers the blast with his ice.

Todoroki survives the war. Together with his family he visits Toya, who is dying on life support, and their short talk about a shared favourite food, soba, brings a moment of peace between the brothers (manga final chapter 430, 2024).

lessons.lesson: Rejecting a parent doesn't have to mean rejecting part of yourself.
lessons.why: Todoroki refuses his fire for years to spite Endeavor, and Izuku's challenge at the Sports Festival shows him the power is his own.

lessons.lesson: Old grudges can sabotage the present.
lessons.why: At the license exam, his clash with Inasa over Endeavor costs them both a pass, and a real rescue is put at risk.

lessons.lesson: Some family wounds can't be fixed, only faced.
lessons.why: Todoroki can't undo what happened to Toya, but he chooses to face Dabi himself and later sits with his dying brother to talk about something as small as soba.

relationships.name: Endeavor (Enji Todoroki)
relationships.detail: The number-two hero married Shoto's mother only to produce an heir strong enough to beat All Might, and his abusive training is why Shoto long refused to use his fire.

relationships.name: Rei Todoroki
relationships.detail: Driven to a breakdown by Endeavor's abuse, Rei poured boiling water on Shoto's face, leaving his scar; after the Sports Festival he finally visits her for the first time in years.

relationships.name: Izuku Midoriya
relationships.detail: In their Sports Festival match, Izuku pushes Shoto to stop rejecting his left side, which changes how Shoto sees his own power.

relationships.name: Katsuki Bakugo
relationships.detail: Bakugo beats a hesitant Shoto in the Sports Festival final and is furious that Shoto held back; the two later retake the provisional license course together.

relationships.name: Tenya Iida
relationships.detail: Shoto joins Izuku in saving Iida from the Hero Killer Stain, and the three bring Stain down together.

relationships.name: Dabi (Toya Todoroki)
relationships.detail: The League of Villains' Dabi reveals himself as Toya, the brother the family believed dead, and Shoto takes it on himself to stop him in the final war.

fights.title: Shoto vs. Izuku at the Sports Festival
fights.summary: Goaded by Izuku, Shoto finally unleashes his left side, and the clash of ice and fire blasts Izuku out of bounds.

fights.title: Shoto vs. Bakugo
fights.summary: In the final, Shoto lets his flames die out mid-attack and is knocked out of the ring, leaving Bakugo an unwanted victory.

fights.title: Shoto, Izuku and Iida vs. Stain
fights.summary: Shoto holds the Hero Killer back until Iida breaks free of Stain's Quirk, and the three students defeat him together.

fights.title: Shoto vs. Dabi

Shoto tells Izuku about his father and the scar on his face.
'Shoto Todoroki: Origin' — he uses his fire in battle for the first time.
Dabi reveals on live broadcast that he is Toya Todoroki.
The heroes announce that Shoto has defeated Dabi.

strength.rank: Recommended U.A. student with a two-sided Quirk
strength.summary: Shoto's Half-Cold Half-Hot Quirk lets him freeze huge areas from his right side and burn from his left. Once he accepts his fire, he combines the two sides, and in the final war he defeats his brother Dabi with Phosphor, an ultimate move he designed himself to stop him.

qualities.detail: She builds her life around her twin sister, Ram, and even tells Subaru that her loyalty to Ram makes her something like a fanatical demon.
Because Subaru carries the scent of the Witch, Rem decides he must belong to the Witch Cult, and in one timeline she hunts him down with her flail.
She sees herself as the lesser twin and has spent years trying to live up to the sister she thinks she failed.
When a swarm of Mabeasts attacks near the village, she lets her oni side take over and fights until she loses control of herself.
Once Subaru convinces her the village children are in danger, she goes with him to find them and heals them herself.

rem-3.backstory: Rem and her older twin, Ram, were born into a village of oni, horned demi-humans among whom the birth of twins was taboo. Because they were twins, each girl had only one horn. Ram was a prodigy and Rem was not, and the gap left Rem with a deep sense of inferiority from childhood. When the Witch Cult attacked their people, Ram's horn was cut off and her great power was lost. Rem felt relief that she no longer had to compete with her sister, and then terrible guilt about that relief, and she has blamed herself ever since. The sisters later came to serve as maids in the mansion of Roswaal L. Mathers, and Rem tried to live the life she believed Ram should have had. Having lost her home to the Witch Cult, she is quick to treat anyone who smells of the Witch as an enemy.

journey.summary: Rem suspects Subaru from the start and kills him in at least one timeline. In the loop that sticks, she goes berserk fighting Mabeasts, Subaru takes a blow meant for her, and when she wakes he tells her to stop looking back and live for the future. From then on she is devoted to him.

journey.stage: The capital and the Witch Cult (Season 1)
journey.summary: Staying with Subaru in the capital while he recovers, she rushes home alone in one timeline to protect him, and in another is tortured by Petelgeuse before using her last strength to free Subaru, begging him to go on living and confessing her love.
When Subaru falls apart and calls himself worthless, Rem refuses to agree, and she declares her love for him, knowing his heart belongs to Emilia, and her belief in him gets him back on his feet.
Riding with Subaru and the allied armies, she fights the White Whale at his side, even launching him into the air on a shard of ice to draw the beast down.
After the battle, Gluttony, one of the Witch Cult's archbishops, eats her name and memories. Rem falls into a coma and everyone except Subaru forgets she ever existed, even Ram.

journey.stage: Asleep, then awake (Seasons 2-3 and the light novels)
journey.summary: Through the anime so far she stays in her coma, with Subaru carrying her and the promise to wake her. In the ongoing light novels she finally wakes as Arc 6 closes, but with no memory of who she was.

lessons.lesson: Comparing yourself to someone you love can poison the love.
lessons.why: Rem's lifelong sense of being the lesser twin turns into guilt so heavy that she spends years living as Ram's replacement instead of as herself.

lessons.lesson: Sometimes believing in someone is the help they need.
lessons.why: In 'From Zero', Rem doesn't fix Subaru's problems; she simply refuses to let him believe he is worthless, and that is enough for him to try again.

lessons.lesson: Loving someone doesn't require them to love you back the same way.
lessons.why: Rem confesses to Subaru knowing he loves Emilia, and keeps fighting at his side anyway.

relationships.name: Subaru Natsuki

relationships.name: Lye Batenkaitos

fights.summary: Rem charges into the woods alone and loses herself in her oni form; Subaru's plan to strike her horn is what brings her back.

fights.title: Holding off the White Whale

fights.title: Bringing down the White Whale

fights.title: Ambushed by Gluttony

Suspecting Subaru of serving the witch, Rem interrogates him brutally in an earlier loop.
Her backstory with Ram, and the moment she falls for Subaru.
Rem refuses to run away with Subaru and tells him she loves him, giving him the will to start again.
Subaru learns that Rem has fallen into a coma and that everyone else has forgotten her.

strength.summary: Rem fights with a spiked meteor hammer and mostly water magic, and when her horn appears she enters a frenzied oni state that lets her take on a forest full of mabeasts by herself. In the White Whale battle she uses an ice shard to fling Subaru toward the whale and catches him as he falls.

qualities.detail: He spends his days reading Weekly Shonen Jump, dodging the rent he owes his landlady Otose, and taking odd jobs only when the Yorozuya is desperate for cash.
His craving for sugar is so strong that his doctor has warned him to cut back, and his first meeting with Shinpachi starts over a spilled parfait.
When a parfait gets knocked over in a family restaurant, he lets Shinpachi take the blame, and he is happy to use dirty tricks if they win a fight faster.
Underneath the slacking, he keeps his own samurai code: the same day he frames Shinpachi, he helps rescue the boy's sister, Otae, from a greedy loan shark.
He gives the runaway Yato girl Kagura a home at the Yorozuya, and he once swore to look after Otose after eating the offerings at her husband's grave.

gintoki-sakata.backstory: Gintoki was taught as a child by Shoyo Yoshida, who opened a school for poor children; Gintoki was its first pupil, and his classmates included Kotaro Katsura and Shinsuke Takasugi. When Shoyo was falsely accused of raising an army and taken away, his students joined the Joi War against the Amanto invaders, hoping to rescue him. Gintoki's silver hair, white coat and terrifying swordsmanship made him a legend called the White Demon. The war ended in defeat. Captured along with Katsura and Takasugi, Gintoki was forced to choose between his friends' lives and his teacher's, and he carried out Shoyo's execution with his own hands. Afterward he drifted into Edo, now ruled under the Amanto, ate the food left at a grave, and promised the widow, Otose, to protect her. He opened the Yorozuya above her bar, handling odd jobs his own way.

journey.summary: Gintoki gains two employees: Shinpachi, a samurai-in-training whose sister Otae is being squeezed by a loan shark, and Kagura, a superhumanly strong Yato girl fleeing the yakuza. He also runs into his old comrade Katsura, now a wanted rebel planting bombs.

After he beats the Shinsengumi chief Kondo in a duel over Otae, the police squad comes looking for the silver-haired samurai, starting a long, prickly rivalry with vice-commander Hijikata and a strange kinship with Okita.

Searching for the missing Katsura, Gintoki discovers that their old friend Takasugi is behind a cursed sword, Benizakura, and he defeats Nizo, the blind killer the sword is slowly consuming. The clash makes it clear that he and Takasugi are now enemies.

Helping the boy Seita reach Hinowa, the woman who raised him and is held captive in the underground district of Yoshiwara, Gintoki takes on its ruler, the Yato warrior Housen, the 'King of the Night', and defeats him with help from sunlight and the district's guards.

The truth about Shoyo's execution comes out, and Gintoki learns that his teacher was the gentler side of the immortal Utsuro, founder of the assassin group Naraku. Gintoki, Katsura and Takasugi end up fighting side by side again.

In the final battle, Takasugi, partly taken over by Utsuro's blood, sacrifices himself to weaken him, and Gintoki strikes the last blow that ends Utsuro for good. Gintoki holds Takasugi as he dies, then returns to life with the Yorozuya (manga ending 2019; film The Final, 2021).

lessons.lesson: Living by your own code matters more than looking respectable.
lessons.why: Gintoki looks like a deadbeat, but from his first chapters he always ends up putting himself on the line for people like Otae and Kagura.

lessons.lesson: Carrying guilt alone pushes people away.
lessons.why: Takasugi spends years hating Gintoki for executing Shoyo, never seeing the regret Gintoki kept to himself, until Takasugi finally understands their teacher's last wish.

lessons.lesson: Silliness and grief can live side by side.
lessons.why: Gintoki jokes, slacks off and eats parfaits while carrying the memory of the war and of his teacher, which is exactly what makes his serious moments hit so hard.

relationships.name: Shinpachi Shimura
relationships.detail: Their first meeting starts with Gintoki pinning a spilled parfait on Shinpachi, then helping save him; Shinpachi ends up working at the Yorozuya and becoming part of Gintoki's found family.

relationships.name: Kagura
relationships.detail: The Yato girl crashes into Gintoki and Shinpachi while running from the yakuza and ends up staying with the Yorozuya.

relationships.name: Toushirou Hijikata
relationships.detail: The Shinsengumi's vice-commander goes looking for the silver-haired samurai who beat his chief, and the two have clashed ever since.

relationships.name: Kotaro Katsura
relationships.relation: childhood friend and old war comrade
relationships.detail: Katsura studied under the same teacher as Gintoki and fought beside him in the Joi War; he is now a wanted rebel.

relationships.name: Shinsuke Takasugi
relationships.detail: Another classmate and Joi War ally, Takasugi now leads the militant Kiheitai, and he and Gintoki meet in a bitter duel during the Shogun Assassination arc.

relationships.name: Shoyo Yoshida
relationships.detail: Shoyo taught Gintoki, Katsura and Takasugi as children; his arrest is what drew the three into the Joi War.

fights.title: Gintoki vs. Kondo
fights.summary: Hired to deal with the man stalking Otae, Gintoki defeats the chief of the Shinsengumi, which puts him on Hijikata's radar.

fights.title: Gintoki vs. Nizō Okada
fights.summary: Gintoki faces the swordsman fused with the living blade Benizakura in their final showdown of the Benizakura arc.

fights.title: Gintoki vs. Housen
fights.summary: With Tsukuyo and the Hyakka fighting beside him, Gintoki strikes Housen down just as Seita opens Yoshiwara's roof to the sun.

fights.title: Gintoki vs. Takasugi
fights.summary: The two former classmates trade blows while remembering their days at Shoyo's school, until Oboro interrupts the duel.

keyEpisodes.why: The first manga chapter adapted: how Gintoki met Shinpachi.
Kagura runs into the pair and the Yorozuya trio comes together.
End of the Benizakura arc, the series' first major serious storyline.
Climax of the Yoshiwara arc against Housen.
Gintoki and Takasugi's long-awaited clash in the Shogun Assassination arc.

strength.rank: Joi War veteran feared as the Shiroyasha ('White Demon')
strength.summary: Despite his lazy act, Gintoki is a war-hardened swordsman whose skill earned him the Shiroyasha name, and he usually fights with a wooden sword. He beats Shinsengumi chief Kondo in their first duel, outlasts the Benizakura-possessed Nizō Okada, and lands the decisive blow on Housen, the Yato who ruled Yoshiwara.

qualities.detail: As leader of Squad 13, she takes charge of the group's missions and worries about every member, not just her own Franxx partner.
Wary of Zero Two's unsavoury reputation and worried for Hiro's safety, she volunteers to pilot Delphinium with him herself.
When she thinks Zero Two is putting too much strain on Hiro's body, she walks straight up to her and tells her to back off.
On a night walk under the stars she is on the verge of telling Hiro how she feels, then lets the moment pass when shooting stars interrupt her.
When Goro is trapped inside a Klaxosaur after ejecting her to safety, she insists on going back and dives into the creature to reach him.

ichigo-f875b8ab-821d-4659-8d8e-5f79e5fd3.backstory: Ichigo, code number 015, is one of the 'parasites', children created artificially and raised in isolation to pilot Franxx mecha in boy-girl pairs against the giant Klaxosaurs. Parasites are not meant to have names or much individuality. As a small child, though, Ichigo was given her name by Hiro, another boy in their group, and she has loved him ever since. Goro is the other friend who completes their childhood trio. Hiro, once a prodigy, later lost his ability to pilot, while Ichigo became the leader of Squad 13 at the Thirteenth Plantation, the city they are assigned to defend, partnered with Goro in the Franxx Delphinium. She has taken on the same naming role herself: her squadmate Ikuno got her name from Ichigo. When the series begins, Ichigo is blunt, emotional, and quietly worried about the boy who named her.

journey.summary: Hiro, a washed-out former prodigy, suddenly pairs up with the notorious Zero Two, and Ichigo tries to pilot with him herself in a mock battle. They connect for a moment before the link breaks, leaving them both frustrated.

Goro ejects her from a captured Delphinium and prepares to blow up its energy tank to take the enemy down with him. Ichigo refuses to leave him, reaches him inside the Klaxosaur, and gets them both out; afterwards Goro tells her how he feels, without asking for an answer.

journey.stage: Keeping Hiro away from Zero Two (episodes 13-14)
journey.summary: Learning that Hiro's body is changing because of his bond with Zero Two, Ichigo and the others bar Zero Two from seeing him. When he tries to follow her anyway, Ichigo kisses him and confesses, but his mind is only on Zero Two.
When she links minds with Hiro, she finds nothing in them but Zero Two, and still she helps him get to her. Accepting how much they mean to each other, she stops standing in their way.

Ikuno confesses that she loves Ichigo, and before Goro leaves to search for survivors, he kisses her. In the epilogue set ten years later, Ichigo is married to Goro and they are expecting their first child.

lessons.lesson: Protecting someone doesn't give you the right to choose for them.
lessons.why: Ichigo keeps Zero Two away from Hiro to protect him, but Hiro chooses Zero Two anyway, and Ichigo only finds peace when she respects that choice.

lessons.lesson: A clear 'no' can set you free.
lessons.why: Once Ichigo sees there is no room for her in Hiro's heart, she can stop waiting, and her life eventually takes a different shape with Goro.

lessons.lesson: Leaders go back for their people.
lessons.why: With Goro trapped inside a Klaxosaur, Ichigo refuses to retreat and dives in after him herself.

relationships.name: Hiro
relationships.detail: As children, Hiro gave Ichigo her name, and she has been fiercely protective of him ever since; when she finally kisses him and confesses, his heart already belongs to Zero Two.

relationships.name: Goro
relationships.detail: Goro has loved Ichigo since childhood and pilots Delphinium with her; years after the war they are married and expecting a child.

relationships.name: Zero Two
relationships.detail: Ichigo distrusts the infamous pilot from the start and confronts her for wearing Hiro down, later trying to keep her away from him altogether.

relationships.name: Ikuno
relationships.detail: Ichigo looks out for Ikuno within Squad 13, and while sick with a fever Ikuno admits to Ichigo that she loves her.

fights.title: Confronting Zero Two
fights.summary: Worried about what piloting Strelizia is doing to Hiro, Ichigo tries to make Zero Two back off, and fails.

fights.title: Rescuing Goro
fights.summary: After Goro ejects her and stays trapped inside a klaxosaur, Ichigo insists on going back in and reaches him just before he can self-destruct.

fights.title: Holding back Strelizia
fights.summary: When Zero Two turns on Hiro, Ichigo's Delphinium grapples with Strelizia at the cost of its arm while she shouts at Hiro to get away.

fights.title: Ichigo's confession
fights.summary: As Hiro moves to follow Zero Two, Ichigo stops him with a kiss and tells him how she feels.

fights.title: Connecting with Hiro
fights.summary: Linking with Hiro to pilot a training unit, Ichigo finds nothing in his mind but Zero Two, and still helps him reach her.

keyEpisodes.why: Debut: Squad 13's leader messages Hiro to show up for the welcome ceremony.
'Triangle Bomb' — Goro's rescue and his confession to Ichigo.
Ichigo confesses her feelings to Hiro.
She accepts that Hiro's heart is with Zero Two.
Finale: Goro kisses Ichigo before setting out, and the epilogue shows them married.

ages.when: Epilogue, eight years after the war

qualities.detail: To win Aunt Mito's blessing for the Hunter Exam, he goes out and catches the 'Lord of the Lake', the island's legendary monster fish.
On the voyage to the exam he lunges after a crewman swept off the deck in a storm, and later whacks Hisoka with his fishing rod to stop him from killing Leorio.
In the exam's final tournament, Hanzo beats him easily and threatens to break his arm, but Gon still refuses to give up.
When Hisoka hands him back his badge as a favour, Gon hates owing him, and he isn't satisfied until he has punched Hisoka in the face and returned the badge.
After Killua's brother pressures him into quitting the exam, Gon heads straight for the Zoldyck family's mountain estate to bring his friend back.

gon-freecss.backstory: Gon grew up on Whale Island, raised by his aunt Mito after his father, Ging, left him in her care and never returned. He spent much of his childhood roaming the island's forests, which sharpened his senses to an almost animal-like degree and gave him an easy way with wild creatures, and he became a skilled fisher. A chance meeting with Kite, a Hunter who turned out to be Ging's student, inspired Gon to follow his absent father into the Hunter's life. Rather than resent Ging for leaving, Gon decided to become a Hunter himself, find his father, and understand what made that life worth choosing over a son. Mito was reluctant to let him leave home, but she gave in once he proved his resolve by catching the Lord of the Lake, the giant fish the islanders spoke of.

journey.summary: Gon befriends Kurapika, Leorio and Killua, snatches Hisoka's target tag with his fishing rod, and refuses to quit against Hanzo, earning his license. When Killua's brother Illumi forces Killua out of the exam, Gon confronts him and vows to fetch his friend.
At Kukuroo Mountain, Gon and his friends train until they can push open the estate's massive Testing Gate, and Gon brings Killua out of the assassin family's home.
Under Wing's teaching he learns Nen and discovers he is an Enhancer. Fighting Hisoka in the arena, he lands the punch he promised himself and returns the badge, then loses the match.
Looking for copies of the game Greed Island, Gon and Killua get drawn into Kurapika's fight with the Phantom Troupe, are captured, and are freed when Kurapika trades the Troupe's leader for them.

Inside Ging's game he trains under Biscuit Krueger, creates his Rock-Paper-Scissors attack, teams up to beat the game master Razor, defeats the murderous Bomber Genthru, and with Killua and Biscuit becomes the first to clear the game.

When Neferpitou attacks, Kite stays behind so Gon and Killua can escape. Gon later learns that Kite is dead and his body has been turned into a puppet. Overcome with rage, Gon makes a Nen vow that turns him briefly into an adult with all of his future power, kills Neferpitou, and is left close to death.

Killua's sibling Alluka heals him. Gon reunites with a reborn Kite, finally sits down with Ging atop the World Tree, parts with Killua, and goes home to Mito. The manga confirms that his vow has cost him the ability to use Nen.

lessons.lesson: Respect can't be accepted as charity.
lessons.why: Gon refuses to treat Hisoka's gift of a badge as a favour he can keep, and only feels even after earning a clean punch on Hisoka at Heavens Arena.

lessons.lesson: Rage that ignores everything else can cost you everything.
lessons.why: Determined to avenge Kite, Gon trades away his future potential to kill Neferpitou, nearly dies, and loses his Nen.

lessons.lesson: The friends you push away are often the ones who save you.
lessons.why: Gon snaps at Killua in his anger over Kite, yet Killua rescues him, gets Alluka to heal him, and receives Gon's apology at the end.

relationships.name: Killua Zoldyck
relationships.detail: Gon and the runaway assassin meet during the Hunter Exam as the only two kids their age, and they stay inseparable through most of the series.

relationships.name: Mito Freecss
relationships.detail: Mito raised Gon on Whale Island after Ging left him, and she lets him go to the Hunter Exam only after he catches the Lord of the Lake.

relationships.name: Ging Freecss
relationships.detail: Gon becomes a Hunter to find the father who left him behind; they finally talk face to face at the very end of the 2011 anime.

relationships.name: Kite
relationships.relation: Ging's apprentice and Gon's role model
relationships.detail: Kite saved Gon from a beast when he was little; Kite's fate at Neferpitou's hands drives Gon's darkest turn.

relationships.name: Hisoka
relationships.detail: Gon snatches Hisoka's exam tag, only for Hisoka to hand it back after rescuing him; Gon repays that debt by punching Hisoka in the face at Heavens Arena.

relationships.name: Neferpitou
relationships.detail: The Chimera Ant Royal Guard who attacked Kite becomes the target of Gon's revenge in the climax of the Chimera Ant arc.

fights.title: Snatching Hisoka's tag
fights.summary: On Zevil Island, Gon waits for Hisoka to strike at someone else, then hooks the magician's tag away with his fishing rod.

fights.title: Gon vs. Hisoka at Heavens Arena
fights.summary: Gon keeps his promise by landing a clean punch on Hisoka and handing back the tag, though he loses the match itself.

fights.title: Gon vs. Genthru
fights.summary: Outmatched in experience, Gon goes off-script in their one-on-one and still defeats the Greed Island bomber.

fights.title: Gon vs. Neferpitou
fights.summary: Learning that Kite cannot be saved, Gon gives up his future to become an adult version of himself and crushes Neferpitou.

keyEpisodes.why: Debut: Gon leaves Whale Island for the Hunter Exam to learn about his father.
Back home, Gon uses Nen to open the box Ging left him and finds a ring, a tape and a game memory card.
Gon's transformation, the darkest turn of the Chimera Ant arc.
Restored to health, Gon finally meets Ging.
Final episode: Gon climbs the World Tree and finally has a real talk with Ging.

strength.rank: Enhancer prodigy
strength.summary: Gon is an Enhancer, a Nen type that makes him extremely strong and quick to heal, and his signature Jajanken turns rock-paper-scissors into a punch, a blade or a ranged blast. He outlasts the experienced bomber Genthru on Greed Island, and in his grief over Kite he forces his body into an adult form that completely overpowers Neferpitou, nearly killing himself.

qualities.detail: When Vaccine Man finishes a furious speech and transforms into something huge, Saitama just waits it out, then ends the fight with one hit. Grand threats barely register with him.
Right after that first easy win he yells in frustration rather than celebrating. Winning every fight in one punch has drained the thrill out of the job he chose.
Supermarket bargains matter to him as much as monsters do. Against Carnage Kabuto, the moment that truly rattles him is realising he may have missed the weekly special sale.
After the Deep Sea King fight he lets the crowd call him a fraud so that the beaten heroes who fought first keep their dignity. He never explains himself to anyone.
Asked how he became so strong, he lists push-ups, sit-ups, squats and a daily run. Nobody believes him, but he isn't trying to impress them either.
He shrugs off Genos's request to be his disciple at first, then agrees as long as Genos signs up as a hero too.

saitama.backstory: Before the yellow suit, Saitama was an unemployed young man trudging from one failed job interview to the next. As a child he had liked hero shows where the good guy wins with a single punch, but adult life had flattened him. Around three years before the story opens, a monster called Crablante went after a cleft-chinned boy, and Saitama, almost on impulse, stepped in and beat it. That fight convinced him to become a hero, just for the fun of it. He then committed to a plain daily routine: a hundred push-ups, a hundred sit-ups, a hundred squats, then a 10 km run, without a heater or air conditioner. About eighteen months in, his hair started falling out. By the first episode he is bald, living alone in an apartment in the near-empty part of Z-City, and too strong to feel anything in a fight.

journey.summary: Saitama flattens monsters with no audience and no recognition. Saving Genos from Mosquito Girl gives him a devoted cyborg disciple and, for the first time, someone sharing his apartment and his routine.

He breaks every physical record at the hero exam but bombs the written test, so he starts near the bottom of C-Class while Genos goes straight to S-Class. His rank climbs slowly because others keep getting the credit.

He shatters a falling meteor and later finishes off the Deep Sea King after several heroes have been beaten trying to stop it. When the crowd turns on the losers, he deliberately makes himself the target of its anger.

journey.stage: Boros and the Dark Matter Thieves (Season 1)
journey.summary: The alien warlord Boros is the first opponent to take several of his blows. Saitama answers Boros's strongest attack with his Serious Punch, and the win leaves him as empty as before.

While the martial artist Garou hunts heroes, the Monster Association kidnaps a Hero Association executive's son and the heroes storm its underground base. During that raid Saitama meets Blast, the top-ranked hero, who warns him about an entity called God. Season 3's second cour is set for January 2027, so the climax is manga-only for now.

Powered by the being called God, Garou kills a string of heroes, Genos among them, to draw Saitama out. Saitama finally fights with real anger, and Garou's power turns out to keep rising as the fight goes on.
With his old apartment destroyed, Saitama is bumped up to rank 39 in A-Class and moved into Hero Association housing in A-City. He is the same deadpan hero, now a little more visible to everyone.

lessons.lesson: Getting what you wanted can still feel empty.
lessons.why: Saitama reached his dream of one-punch strength and then screamed in frustration after beating Vaccine Man. The show treats his boredom as a real problem, not a punchline.

lessons.lesson: Good work doesn't need a crowd.
lessons.why: After the Deep Sea King he accepts being booed so the injured heroes are spared. He doesn't correct the story afterwards, either.

lessons.lesson: Ordinary habits add up.
lessons.why: His power is played for laughs, but the story keeps returning to the same three years of daily push-ups and runs. The routine was boring, and he kept it anyway.

lessons.lesson: Even the most relaxed person has a line.
lessons.why: Saitama shrugs off insults, rankings and alien warlords, but Garou destroying Genos's core is what finally makes him fight in anger. His calm was never the same as not caring.

relationships.name: Genos
relationships.detail: A cyborg hero who asks to become Saitama's student after seeing him swat Mosquito Girl away, then shows up at his door to make it official.

relationships.name: Speed-o'-Sound Sonic
relationships.detail: A ninja who decides Saitama is his nemesis after their first run-in; Saitama barely remembers him and keeps knocking him out with almost no effort.

relationships.name: Mumen Rider
relationships.detail: The bicycle-riding C-Class hero whose hopeless stand against the Deep Sea King moves Saitama, who catches him and finishes the fight for him.

relationships.name: Bang
relationships.detail: The elderly S-Class martial artist welcomes Saitama and Genos to his dojo and warns them about Garou, the star pupil who turned on his school.

relationships.name: King
relationships.detail: The famous 'strongest man' is really just an everyday gamer whose reputation was built on monsters Saitama quietly killed; Saitama keeps his secret and the two play video games together.

relationships.name: Fubuki
relationships.detail: The leader of the Blizzard Group tries to force Saitama into her faction; he shrugs off her psychic attacks and tells her that leaning on underlings will leave her with no one to rely on.

fights.title: Saitama vs. Vaccine Man
fights.summary: The series opens with a giant monster born from pollution, which Saitama pops with a single bored punch.

fights.title: Sparring with Genos
fights.summary: Genos demands a serious practice match; Saitama dodges everything, leaves afterimages, and stops his punch just short, wrecking the scenery behind his student instead.

fights.title: Saitama vs. Speed-o'-Sound Sonic
fights.summary: Sonic forces a rematch by attacking the city; Saitama bites his sword in two and puts him down almost instantly.

fights.title: Stopping the meteor
fights.summary: After Genos, Bang and Metal Knight fail to stop a meteor falling on City Z, Saitama leaps up and shatters it with one punch.

fights.title: Saitama vs. the Deep Sea King
fights.summary: Arriving just as Mumen Rider collapses, Saitama ends the Seafolk leader in one blow, then lets the crowd think he got lucky so the beaten heroes keep their dignity.

fights.title: Saitama vs. Boros
fights.summary: The alien conqueror throws everything at Saitama, even kicking him to the Moon, but Saitama returns and answers Boros's strongest beam with a Serious Punch.

keyEpisodes.why: Debut, plus the flashback to the crab monster and the training routine that made him too strong to enjoy fighting.
He passes the Hero Association exam but lands in C-Class because of his weak written test score.
His Deep Sea King victory, and his choice to take the blame so the defeated heroes are not mocked, define his quiet kind of heroism.
The Boros fight is the closest anyone has come to giving him a real battle.
Saitama rescues King and learns the truth behind the 'strongest man' title, starting their friendship.
Entered in a martial arts tournament under Charanko's name, he knocks out the bully Bakuzan with one punch.

strength.rank: Strongest character in the series
strength.summary: Saitama ends nearly every fight with one ordinary punch and has never been seriously hurt in the anime. He smashed a meteor heading for City Z, flattened the Deep Sea King with a single blow, and against Boros he leapt back from the Moon after being kicked there, then cancelled the alien's planet-scale beam with one Serious Punch.

qualities.detail: Hange calls him a clean freak, and he lives up to it: he wipes blood off his blades mid-battle and expects any base he occupies to be scrubbed spotless.
At Eren's military trial he beats the chained boy in front of the court. It looks cruel, but it is a calculated show that persuades the judges the Survey Corps can control Eren.
In the same courtroom he mocks the Military Police for never having faced a Titan and suggests they enlist in the Survey Corps themselves if they think they can do better.
In the forest, with the Female Titan closing in, he tells Eren that nobody knows the right call until afterwards and lets him choose between transforming and trusting the squad.
His blade work and control of vertical maneuvering equipment earn him the title of humanity's strongest soldier, and he cuts through Titans that wipe out whole squads.

levi.backstory: Levi grew up in the Underground City beneath the capital, born to Kuchel Ackerman, a young woman scraping by in poverty there. When she died, her older brother Kenny found the boy alone beside her bed and took him in for a while, teaching him to handle a knife and survive among violent people before abruptly leaving. Levi grew into a skilled thief who used stolen maneuvering gear, working with his friend Furlan Church and later a girl named Isabel Magnolia. Commander Erwin Smith's Survey Corps caught the trio and offered them a deal: enlist instead of facing punishment. Levi joined meaning to kill Erwin for a secret employer, but on his first expedition Titans killed Furlan and Isabel. Learning that the plot had been pointless all along, he chose to stay with Erwin, and the prequel No Regrets is built around that decision.

journey.summary: Levi enters as the Survey Corps' strongest soldier and takes custody of Eren after the trial, forming the Special Operations Squad to protect him and, if needed, kill him.
The Female Titan wipes out his hand-picked squad while he is away. With Mikasa he snatches Eren back from her, injuring his leg in the process.
Hunted by the royal government, he faces Kenny Ackerman, his uncle and old teacher. The dying Kenny hands him the Titan serum and finally explains their family name.

Erwin leads a suicide charge so Levi can reach the Beast Titan, Zeke, whom he cuts down but fails to kill. Given one dose of serum, he uses it on Armin rather than the dying Erwin, letting his commander rest.

Holding a captured Zeke in a forest, Levi rigs a Thunder Spear to his prisoner to stop him transforming. Zeke sets it off himself, and the blast leaves Levi scarred and missing two fingers until Hange finds him and gets him away.

journey.stage: Battle of Heaven and Earth (Final Season)
journey.summary: Barely healed, Levi joins the alliance with former Marleyan enemies to stop Eren's Rumbling. He finally kills Zeke, keeping his promise to Erwin.
Three years later he lives in Marley in a wheelchair, looked after by Gabi and Falco, one of the few original veterans left.

lessons.lesson: Choose, then own the choice.
lessons.why: In the forest Levi tells Eren nobody can know the right answer beforehand. Eren trusts his squad, they die, and Levi never pretends the decision came with a guarantee.

lessons.lesson: Sometimes kindness means letting go.
lessons.why: With one dose of serum, Levi could have saved Erwin. He saw how tired his friend was and gave it to Armin instead.

lessons.lesson: A promise can outlast the person it was made to.
lessons.why: Levi swore to Erwin that the Beast Titan would die by his hand. Years later, scarred and barely standing, he finishes the job.

lessons.lesson: Where you start doesn't decide who you become.
lessons.why: Raised in the slums by a killer, he became the person soldiers trusted most. Joining the Survey Corps began as a con and ended as a calling.

relationships.name: Erwin Smith
relationships.detail: Erwin pulled Levi out of a life of crime in the Underground and into the Survey Corps, and Levi became the officer he trusted most.

relationships.name: Eren Yeager
relationships.detail: Levi takes responsibility for Eren after the Battle of Trost, beating him in front of the military court to prove the Scouts can control him, then guarding him in the Special Operations Squad.

relationships.name: Petra Ral
relationships.detail: One of the hand-picked soldiers of his Special Operations Squad, who guards Eren alongside her squadmates during the 57th expedition.

relationships.name: Hange Zoë
relationships.detail: A long-time Survey Corps comrade who teases his obsession with cleanliness; after the forest explosion Hange drags the badly wounded Levi to safety and patches him up.

relationships.name: Kenny Ackerman
relationships.detail: The serial killer who raised Levi as a boy in the Underground returns as an enemy; dying, he reveals he is the brother of Levi's late mother.

relationships.name: Mikasa Ackerman
relationships.detail: They are two of the last known Ackermans, which explains the shared, almost superhuman fighting ability of these two hard-headed soldiers.

relationships.name: Zeke Yeager
relationships.detail: The Beast Titan's barrage wipes out Erwin's suicide charge at Shiganshina; Levi promises Erwin he will kill the Beast Titan and spends years trying to keep that vow.

fights.title: Rescue in Trost
fights.summary: As the battle for Trost winds down, Levi drops in and kills the Titans closing in on Eren and his friends.

fights.title: Levi and Mikasa vs. the Female Titan
fights.summary: Teaming up with Mikasa, Levi carves up the Female Titan at blinding speed and frees Eren from her jaws.

fights.title: Escaping Kenny's ambush
fights.summary: Hunted through the streets by Kenny and the Interior Squad, Levi fights his way free after his team is gunned down.

fights.title: Levi vs. the Beast Titan
fights.summary: Hidden by Erwin's suicide charge, Levi reaches the Beast Titan, shreds it and cuts Zeke out of the nape.

fights.title: Recapturing Zeke in the forest
fights.summary: After Zeke turns Levi's own soldiers into Titans, Levi cuts through all of them and brings the Beast Titan down with Thunder Spears.

fights.title: The final strike on Zeke
fights.summary: In the last battle Zeke lets Levi decapitate him, halting the Rumbling, before Levi blasts open the Founding Titan's mouth for Mikasa.

keyEpisodes.why: His staged beating of Eren in court wins the Survey Corps custody of humanity's new weapon.
His rescue of Eren from the Female Titan is the first full showcase of his skill.
The dying Kenny tells Levi they are family, reshaping Levi's understanding of his own past.
With one dose of Titan serum, Levi decides to let Erwin rest and saves Armin instead.
Zeke sets off the Thunder Spear fixed to his own body, leaving Levi gravely wounded.
Levi finally keeps his vow to Erwin by killing Zeke.

strength.rank: Humanity's strongest soldier
strength.summary: Levi carries the official nickname of humanity's strongest soldier and leads the Survey Corps' elite squad. In Trost he arrives out of nowhere to cut down two Titans cornering Eren and Armin, and during the 57th expedition he slices the exhausted Female Titan apart faster than she can harden her skin, pulling Eren out of her mouth despite hurting his leg.

qualities.detail: He first shows up as a cheeky kid on a skateboard, treating the deadly Hunter Exam like a game he joined on a whim. Snacks, especially chocolate, are never far from his mind.
In the Trick Tower, a serial killer challenges the group to a fight to the death. Killua finishes it in an instant, a reminder of what his family trained him to be.
Gon is the first real friend he has ever had, and Killua repeatedly puts Gon's safety ahead of his own, from the exam onwards.
He reads situations quickly and plans several moves ahead, often working out an opponent's trick or a game's rules before Gon does.
When his brother Illumi confronts him during the exam finals, the confident boy freezes. Years of conditioning have taught him to fear anyone stronger than himself.

killua-zoldyck.backstory: Killua is Silva and Kikyo Zoldyck's third child; his parents lead a famous family of assassins living on Kukuroo Mountain. Marked early as the most gifted child in generations, he was put through brutal training from the age of three: poison until his body could shrug it off, electric shocks until he barely felt them, and lessons in killing that left him with more victims than most career criminals. His older brother Illumi took a special interest in him, and secretly planted a needle in his head so he would always run from fights he might lose. He also hid a family secret involving his sibling Alluka, whose strange wish-granting power the family feared. At eleven, tired of killing, he lashed out at his mother and his brother Milluki and ran away from home, signing up for the Hunter Exam mostly for fun.

journey.summary: He bonds with Gon, Kurapika and Leorio and breezes through the early phases. In the finals Illumi, disguised as Gittarackur, tells him he can never have friends; shaken, Killua kills another candidate and is disqualified, then goes home.
Back on Kukuroo Mountain he lets himself be punished for leaving. When he learns his friends have come for him, his father lets him go, and he rejoins Gon.
Climbing the fighting tower to earn money, he and Gon learn Nen from Wing. Killua discovers he is a Transmuter and begins turning his aura into electricity.

He helps Kurapika against the Phantom Troupe, then enters Greed Island, where Biscuit Krueger's training sharpens him. He develops his electric abilities and, during a break from the game, retakes the Hunter Exam and passes easily; he and Gon become among the first players to clear Greed Island.

Facing enemies far stronger than him, he finds himself fleeing on instinct. To protect Gon he discovers and pulls out Illumi's needle, then watches helplessly as Gon's grief over Kite turns into something frightening.

With Gon near death after his fight with Neferpitou, Killua defies his family and Illumi to bring Alluka out and use her power to heal him. Once Gon recovers, Killua chooses to travel with Alluka instead, where the 2011 anime ends.

lessons.lesson: Upbringing explains you; it doesn't own you.
lessons.why: Killua was raised to kill without feeling, yet he walks away from it at eleven. The rest of the story is him slowly proving that choice was real.

lessons.lesson: Fear can be planted by others.
lessons.why: His habit of running from strong enemies turns out to be Illumi's needle, literally lodged in his head. Pulling it out is one of his biggest moments of growth.

lessons.lesson: Real friends tell you when you're wrong.
lessons.why: After Gon is healed, Killua makes him apologise for how badly he treated people during the Chimera Ant crisis. Loyalty, for Killua, includes honesty.

lessons.lesson: Sometimes caring for someone means leaving.
lessons.why: Killua and Gon part ways at the end of the anime so Killua can protect Alluka. He chooses the person who needs him most over his own comfort.

relationships.name: Gon Freecss
relationships.detail: The two boys meet as the same-age rookies of the Hunter Exam, and Gon becomes the first friend Killua has ever had outside his family.

relationships.name: Kurapika
relationships.detail: A fellow Hunter Exam examinee; while Killua and Gon are held by the Phantom Troupe, Killua works out that the chain user the Troupe is hunting is Kurapika.

relationships.name: Leorio Paradinight
relationships.detail: Another member of the exam foursome, who travels with Gon to the Zoldyck estate to bring Killua back.

relationships.name: Illumi Zoldyck
relationships.detail: Illumi shows up disguised in the exam, frightens Killua into giving up, and turns out to have planted a needle in his head long ago to make him flee from strong enemies.

relationships.name: Silva Zoldyck
relationships.detail: The head of the assassin clan lets Killua leave home to rejoin his friends, provided Killua never betrays them.

relationships.name: Biscuit Krueger
relationships.detail: The Nen master Killua and Gon ask to train them on Greed Island, who drills them in the fundamentals while they play through the game.

relationships.name: Alluka Zoldyck
relationships.detail: Killua frees the sibling his family keeps locked away so Alluka's wish-granting power can heal Gon, then sets off to protect Alluka.

fights.title: Killua vs. Johness
fights.summary: In the Trick Tower, Killua faces a notorious mass murderer and wins in an instant by tearing out his heart.

fights.title: The final round of the Hunter Exam
fights.summary: Confronted by his brother Illumi, Killua forfeits, then kills the examinee Bodoro and disqualifies himself.

fights.title: Killua vs. Zushi
fights.summary: At Heavens Arena, a beginner who keeps getting back up unsettles Killua with a mysterious aura, his first brush with Nen.

fights.title: Dodgeball vs. Razor
fights.summary: Killua, Gon and Hisoka team up to beat the Greed Island game master in a brutal dodgeball match, at the cost of Killua's hands.

fights.title: Killua vs. Rammot
fights.summary: Torn between fleeing and saving Gon, Killua finds Illumi's needle in his head, removes it and dispatches the Chimera Ant easily.

fights.title: Killua vs. Menthuthuyoupi
fights.summary: Killua stuns the Royal Guard with a bolt of lightning just before he can kill Knuckle, then steps in to fight him himself.

keyEpisodes.why: On the exam airship Killua casually tells Gon that his family are assassins.
Illumi's pressure breaks him and he walks away from the exam, setting up the rescue arc.
His father agrees to let him leave home to be with his friends.
Removing Illumi's needle frees him from the fear that has controlled his fighting.
He goes home to ask for Alluka's help to save Gon.
Killua and Gon go their separate ways, promising to meet again.

strength.rank: One of the most gifted assassins the Zoldyck family has produced
strength.summary: Raised from birth as a killing machine, Killua pulls out a serial killer's heart in the Hunter Exam before anyone sees him move. After learning Nen he becomes a Transmuter who turns his aura into electricity, enough to stun the Royal Guard Menthuthuyoupi and hold him off.

qualities.detail: In the first episode he takes over a losing chess game against a noble and turns it around in minutes, opening by moving his king. The same habit of reading a whole board drives everything he does as Zero.
Nearly every plan he makes comes back to Nunnally, his blind younger sister who cannot walk. He wants a world where she can live safely and openly.
At Ashford Academy he plays a sociable, slightly lazy student-council member. Behind the Zero mask he is commanding, theatrical and ruthless.
He blames his father, the Emperor, for failing to protect his mother and for discarding him and Nunnally. That anger fuels his rebellion from the very start.
Handed the Geass in the Shinjuku Ghetto, he immediately uses it and takes command of a beaten resistance cell, betting everything on a plan he improvises on the spot.

lelouch-lamperouge.backstory: Lelouch was born into Britannia's imperial family as a prince, son of Emperor Charles zi Britannia and Marianne vi Britannia, a commoner who had risen to knighthood before becoming an imperial consort. When Marianne was murdered inside the palace, his younger sister Nunnally was left blind and unable to walk. Ten-year-old Lelouch confronted his father, accused him of leaving her unprotected and renounced his place in the succession. The Emperor then sent both children to Japan as political hostages, where they stayed with the Kururugi family and Lelouch became close friends with Suzaku Kururugi. Britannia invaded anyway, renaming Japan as Area 11. Officially dead after the war, the siblings were quietly taken in by the Ashford family and live under the surname Lamperouge. Seven years later Lelouch is a bored, brilliant student who hustles nobles at chess and nurses a vow to destroy Britannia.

journey.summary: Caught up in a military crackdown, he meets the immortal C.C., who gives him the Geass of absolute obedience. He uses it to turn the battle, then corners his half-brother Clovis, questions him about Marianne's death, and kills him.
Wearing a mask as Zero, he rescues Suzaku from a framed murder charge and builds his Black Knights into a popular force fighting Britannian rule, while still attending school as Lelouch.

His Geass gets stuck on, and an offhand joke makes his half-sister Euphemia order a massacre of the Japanese she had promised to protect. He kills her, uses the tragedy to launch the Black Rebellion, then abandons the battle when Nunnally is kidnapped and ends the season facing Suzaku at gunpoint.
A year later the Emperor has rewritten his memories and planted Rolo as a fake younger brother. C.C. restores him, and he retakes command of the Black Knights, winning Rolo over.
He forms the United Federation of Nations, but a FLEIJA blast he indirectly causes seems to kill Nunnally. Schneizel turns the Black Knights against him, and Rolo dies saving him.

After erasing his parents in their plan to wipe out individuality, he seizes the throne with Suzaku as his knight. Having made himself the world's single hated tyrant, he lets Suzaku, dressed as Zero, kill him in public so the world can unite in peace.

lessons.lesson: Power used carelessly can't be taken back.
lessons.why: One joking line under a Geass he couldn't switch off turned Euphemia into a killer. Lelouch spends the rest of the series living with the cost.

lessons.lesson: Ends and means can't be fully separated.
lessons.why: He builds the Black Knights on lies and Geass, and when the truth leaks out they turn on him. The plan that works in the end is the one where he pays the price himself.

lessons.lesson: Taking responsibility can mean taking the blame.
lessons.why: In the Zero Requiem he makes himself the target of the whole world's hatred and dies for it, so others can start over without him.

lessons.lesson: Love can blind a strategist.
lessons.why: He walks off the Black Rebellion's battlefield the moment Nunnally is taken, dooming his own uprising. His biggest strength and biggest weakness are the same person.

relationships.name: Nunnally vi Britannia
relationships.detail: Left blind by the attack that killed their mother, Nunnally is the person Lelouch most wants to protect, and her safety drives many of his choices.

relationships.name: Suzaku Kururugi
relationships.detail: His closest friend from their childhood in Japan, who chooses to change Britannia from within and becomes the pilot of the Lancelot, the machine that keeps wrecking Zero's plans.

relationships.name: C.C.
relationships.detail: The mysterious green-haired girl who gives Lelouch the Geass in Shinjuku and stays at his side as his secretive partner.

relationships.name: Kallen Stadtfeld
relationships.detail: A classmate who secretly fights in the Japanese resistance and becomes head of the Black Knights' elite unit, piloting the Guren for Zero.

relationships.name: Shirley Fenette
relationships.detail: A cheerful friend from the student council whose father dies in the Narita landslide Zero set off; Lelouch erases her memories of him to spare her.

relationships.name: Euphemia li Britannia
relationships.detail: A kind-hearted princess whose plan for a special zone for the Japanese nearly ends his rebellion, until his Geass slips out of control at the ceremony.

relationships.name: Rolo Lamperouge
relationships.detail: After the Emperor rewrites Lelouch's memories, Rolo is planted at his side as a 'brother' to watch him, and Lelouch has to win him over.

relationships.name: Charles zi Britannia
relationships.detail: The Emperor of Britannia, who exiled Lelouch and Nunnally to Japan after their mother's death and became the target of his revenge.

fights.title: The Shinjuku Ghetto
fights.summary: Moments after receiving the Geass, Lelouch takes command of a cornered resistance cell and turns the battle against Prince Clovis's army.

fights.title: Battle for Narita
fights.summary: The Black Knights bury the Britannian forces with an engineered landslide and corner Cornelia, until Suzaku's Lancelot crashes the party.

fights.title: The Black Rebellion
