journey.summary: He recruits Atsushi into the Agency and steers him through his first clashes with the Port Mafia. He allows himself to be captured and taunts Akutagawa, his former subordinate, from his cell.
The story flashes back to his Mafia days with Oda and Ango, ending with Oda's death and Dazai's decision to leave.

When the American organisation known as the Guild attacks Yokohama, Dazai helps broker a temporary truce that puts the Agency and the Port Mafia on the same side and briefly reunites with Chuuya as Double Black.

Fyodor Dostoyevsky, leader of the Rats in the House of the Dead, pits the Agency and the Port Mafia against one another. Dazai is shot and hospitalised, then tracks Fyodor down with help from the Guild and has him arrested.

Framed and hunted by the government's Hunting Dogs, the Agency scatters, and Dazai ends up in the European prison Meursault alongside Fyodor. He escapes with Sigma's help as part of a plan with Ango, then is shot by a seemingly turned Chuuya.
The anime reveals that Chuuya only pretended to be a vampire and faked Dazai's death while the plan to stop Fyodor played out. The manga continues as of November 2026, with Dazai alive.

lessons.lesson: One friend's words can redirect a life.
lessons.why: Oda's last request is the reason Dazai leaves the Mafia. Everything he does at the Agency is an attempt to honour it.

lessons.lesson: People can change sides for good.
lessons.why: Once the Mafia's youngest executive, he now uses the same intellect to protect Yokohama. The story keeps testing whether that change is real.

lessons.lesson: Believing in someone can help them believe in themselves.
lessons.why: Dazai backs Atsushi when the boy thinks he's worthless. That faith helps turn a hungry orphan into a capable agent.

lessons.lesson: Humour isn't the same as being okay.
lessons.why: His jokes about death mask real darkness in his past. The series lets you laugh with him while showing that the pain under it is serious.

relationships.name: Atsushi Nakajima
relationships.detail: Dazai is fished out of a river by the starving Atsushi, then brings him into the Armed Detective Agency and guides him like a mentor.

relationships.name: Doppo Kunikida
relationships.detail: His rule-bound partner at the Agency, endlessly exasperated by Dazai's slacking and suicide jokes.

relationships.name: Ryuunosuke Akutagawa
relationships.detail: Dazai trained Akutagawa harshly in the Port Mafia, and Akutagawa still craves his approval and resents Atsushi for receiving it.

relationships.name: Chuuya Nakahara
relationships.detail: Together they were the Port Mafia's feared duo Double Black; they bicker constantly but still fight as a perfect team when it counts.

relationships.name: Sakunosuke Oda
relationships.detail: A low-ranking mafioso who refused to kill; his dying advice to live as someone who saves people pushes Dazai to leave the Port Mafia.

relationships.name: Fyodor Dostoyevsky
relationships.detail: Fyodor, who heads the terrorist group known as the Rats, is Dazai's match in cunning, and their battle of wits spans several seasons, including a showdown inside a prison.

fights.title: Stopping the tiger
fights.summary: When Atsushi turns into the man-eating tiger under the full moon, Dazai cancels the transformation with a touch of No Longer Human.

fights.title: Dazai vs. Chuuya in the Mafia cell
fights.summary: Having let himself be captured and chained in a Port Mafia cell, Dazai faces off with his old partner Chuuya, who wants to know what he is really planning.

fights.title: Double Black vs. Lovecraft
fights.summary: Dazai and Chuuya reunite as Double Black; Dazai lets Chuuya unleash Corruption on the monstrous Lovecraft, then touches him to stop the rampage.

fights.title: Outthinking Fyodor
fights.summary: Dazai predicts Fyodor's moves, uses Fitzgerald's grip on the city's cameras, and arrives with police backup to end the Cannibalism crisis.

fights.title: Escape from Meursault
fights.summary: Locked in a prison with Fyodor and forced into a game only one can win, Dazai walks out with help from Ango, leaving his rival trapped.

keyEpisodes.why: Debut, floating down the river in one of his suicide attempts before taking Atsushi in.
Akutagawa lets slip that Dazai was once part of the Port Mafia.
Oda dies in his arms, the turning point that sends Dazai to the side of the light.
A flashback to how he first met Chuuya as a teenager in the Port Mafia.
Chuuya appears to shoot him dead in the prison, a staged death that sets up the season's last twist.

ages.when: Dazai, Chuuya, Fifteen Years Old flashback

qualities.detail: Dropped into a fantasy kingdom in his tracksuit, he strikes poses and talks like the hero of a game. The swagger covers how little he can actually do.
He throws himself into Emilia's search for her stolen insignia within minutes of meeting her, with no plan and no fighting ability.
Each time Return by Death resets him, he goes back in and tries again to save the people he has just watched die, even when it breaks him.
A force connected to the Witch of Envy stops him whenever he tries to explain his loops, so he carries every death alone while others grow suspicious of him.
Without magic or swordsmanship, he relies on stamina from his daily workouts, quick reflexes and whatever he learned in earlier loops.

subaru-natsuki.backstory: Subaru Natsuki was an ordinary Japanese teenager who had drifted into a shut-in life. Growing up, he wanted to be like his father, a popular and respected man in their community, and for a while he played the energetic kid who could do anything. As he got older he realised he couldn't live up to that image, and the gap ate at him until he stopped going to school and stayed home. The Sanctuary trials later show that his parents, especially his mother, never stopped caring, and that he had never actually told them how he felt. Despite being a hikikomori he kept exercising every day with basic bodyweight drills. One night, walking home from a convenience store with snacks in hand, he was suddenly pulled into the Kingdom of Lugunica, where he would discover his only power: dying and coming back.

journey.summary: He meets Emilia and dies alongside her at the hands of the assassin Elsa, discovering Return by Death. After failed loops he finally calls for help, and the knight Reinhard arrives to save them.
Working as a servant, he keeps dying to a curse and to Rem, who suspects him. He learns to see the household as real people and wins Rem's trust by saving the village from cursed beasts.

journey.stage: Arc 3: Royal Selection and the White Whale (Season 1)
journey.summary: His need for validation leads him to humiliate himself and Emilia at the Royal Selection. After many failed loops he breaks down to Rem, who calls him her hero; he then builds an alliance that kills the White Whale and defeats the Sin Archbishop Petelgeuse, though Rem is left in a coma.

Facing trials about his past and his habit of treating his own life as worthless, he learns to rely on his friends. He saves both the Sanctuary and the mansion, persuades Beatrice to live as his contracted spirit and is knighted by Emilia.
A year later the Witch Cult attacks the water city of Priestella. Subaru rallies the citizens with a speech and works out how to break Regulus's invulnerability.
Seeking a cure for the Cult's victims at a remote tower, Subaru suddenly loses every memory of his life in Lugunica and has to work out who he has become.

lessons.lesson: Asking for help is a strength.
lessons.why: Subaru's very first win comes when he stops trying to be the hero and simply yells for help. The lesson keeps coming back each arc.

lessons.lesson: Admitting your flaws can be the turning point.
lessons.why: He only breaks out of his worst loops in Arc 3 after confessing to Rem how small and useless he feels. Her answer gives him something to stand on.

lessons.lesson: Your own life counts too.
lessons.why: In the Sanctuary he treats dying as a tool and is confronted with how much his deaths hurt others. Learning to value himself is a big part of his growth.

lessons.lesson: Respect people as people, not plot devices.
lessons.why: Early on he acts like the star of a fantasy game. He makes progress only when he starts treating Rem, Ram and the others as people with their own reasons.

relationships.name: Emilia
relationships.detail: The half-elf royal candidate who helps him on his first day in the new world; Subaru appoints himself her knight and keeps dying to protect her.

relationships.name: Rem
relationships.detail: The maid who first suspects him, then falls for him after he saves her; her faith in him pulls Subaru out of his lowest point.

relationships.name: Ram
relationships.detail: Rem's sharp-tongued twin, who works alongside Subaru at Roswaal's mansion and supplies key information about her sister.

relationships.name: Julius Euclius
relationships.detail: The knight thrashes Subaru in a one-sided duel after Subaru insults the royal guard, but later fights beside him against Petelgeuse, lending him his spirit.

relationships.name: Petelgeuse Romanee-Conti
relationships.detail: The Archbishop of Sloth whose cult attacks the mansion again and again, and who even tries to possess Subaru's body.

relationships.name: Otto Suwen
relationships.detail: The merchant who once abandoned him on the road later stands up for Subaru in the Sanctuary, insisting he helps because they are friends.

relationships.name: Beatrice
relationships.detail: The library's grumpy guardian spends centuries waiting for 'that person' until Subaru asks her to choose him instead, and she becomes his partner.

fights.title: The first loop
fights.summary: Subaru is killed on his first day in the new world and wakes up back at the fruit stall, discovering his Return by Death.

fights.title: Subaru vs. Julius
fights.summary: After declaring himself Emilia's knight, Subaru is challenged to a wooden-sword duel and beaten badly by the far more skilled Julius.

fights.title: The White Whale
fights.summary: Riding with Rem on Patrasche, Subaru yells out his secret to draw the White Whale toward himself and away from injured soldiers.

fights.title: Defeating Petelgeuse
fights.summary: With Julius seeing the Unseen Hands through his eyes, Subaru breaks Petelgeuse's hold on him and finally burns the Archbishop away.

fights.title: Subaru vs. Garfiel
fights.summary: Using Invisible Providence, Subaru beats the much stronger Garfiel one-on-one and helps him face the truth about his mother.

fights.title: Breaking Regulus's Authority
fights.summary: In Priestella, Subaru uses Invisible Providence to cut the link between Emilia and Regulus, finally making the Archbishop of Greed vulnerable.

keyEpisodes.why: Debut and first death in the new world.
Rem dies protecting him from the Witch Cult, driving Subaru to the edge of madness.
Rem's confession convinces him to start over 'from zero'.
The first season's final victory over Petelgeuse.
He begs Beatrice to pick him over her endless wait, and she becomes his contracted partner.

qualities.detail: He scores exactly 50 points on every subject of the entrance exam. It's a perfect way to stay invisible, and it makes his teacher and the student council president suspicious.
Before the first midterm he quietly buys an old test from an upperclassman with private points, reading the school's rules as a toolkit rather than a limit.
When Sudo is at risk of expulsion over a fight, Kiyotaka works the problem from the shadows and lets Suzune and others take the visible role.
His self-introduction on day one is so clumsy that Suzune openly mocks it. Making ordinary friends is genuinely hard for him.
His inner narration treats classmates as pieces to be used. He tells himself that winning matters more than how people feel about it.

kiyotaka-ayanokouji.backstory: Kiyotaka is the son of a powerful man who runs a secret facility called the White Room, where children were put through relentless tests and training designed to produce people with near-superhuman abilities. Kiyotaka was raised there and was the only one to meet every one of its standards. He grew up with little ordinary human contact, and his father's lessons shaped his view that other people are tools for reaching a goal. Wanting a taste of freedom, he enrolled at the Advanced Nurturing High School, a government-run school cut off from the outside world, where his father cannot easily reach him. He deliberately hid his abilities on the entrance exam, scoring exactly half marks in every subject, and landed in Class D, the lowest-ranked class. His father later tries to pressure the school into expelling him, which tells Kiyotaka that his escape is far from secure.

journey.summary: Class D blows its monthly points and learns that classes rise and fall by merit. Kiyotaka helps keep the weakest students from expulsion, including spending points to save Sudo after a failed test.

journey.stage: Sudo's case and the island exam (Season 1)
journey.summary: He uncovers a witness, Airi Sakura, to clear Sudo of a staged assault, then wins the week-long survival exam on an uninhabited island for Class D through a plan nobody else sees until the results. He also learns that his father has asked the school to expel him.

journey.stage: Cruise ship, Sports Festival and Ryuen (Season 2)
journey.summary: As exams grow more complex, Class C's leader Kakeru Ryuen hunts for the hidden strategist in Class D. When Ryuen corners Kei Karuizawa on the school rooftop, Kiyotaka confronts him in person and beats him and his group, and Ryuen steps down as his class's leader. Around the same time his father visits the school and offers to take him out; Kiyotaka refuses.

An acting director named Tsukishiro arrives and starts manipulating special exams to get Kiyotaka expelled. Kiyotaka keeps steering Class D from the background through the year's final exams, and by the start of second year he and Kei are secretly dating.

journey.stage: Second year (light novels; anime from Season 4)
journey.summary: A White Room student is planted among the new first-years and a bounty is placed on his expulsion, while Tsukishiro keeps up the pressure. The light novels are ongoing, Season 4 aired in April-June 2026, with a fifth season on the way.

lessons.lesson: Rules reward people who read them closely.
lessons.why: Kiyotaka's early wins come from understanding the school's point system better than everyone else, like buying an old test that was never forbidden.

lessons.lesson: Treating people as tools has a cost.
lessons.why: The series lets you admire his plans while showing how coldly he uses classmates, and whether he can change is one of its big questions.

lessons.lesson: Credit isn't the same as impact.
lessons.why: He lets Suzune and others take the spotlight for victories he planned. The show treats influence as something that can stay invisible.

lessons.lesson: Freedom has to be defended.
lessons.why: He enrolled to get away from the White Room, and his father's attempts to pull him back turn that freedom into something he has to fight for.

relationships.name: Suzune Horikita
relationships.detail: His aloof seatmate in Class D; Ayanokouji quietly feeds her ideas and lets her take the credit so he can stay unnoticed.

relationships.name: Airi Sakura
relationships.detail: A shy classmate who works up the courage to ask Ayanokouji out, then loses her nerve when he arrives.

relationships.name: Sae Chabashira
relationships.detail: Class D's teacher sees through his act and pressures him to aim for Class A, using the fact that someone has asked for his expulsion.

relationships.name: Atsuomi Ayanokouji
relationships.detail: The man who demanded the school expel Ayanokouji turns out to be his father, whom he has decided to defy.

relationships.name: Kei Karuizawa
relationships.detail: On the cruise, Ayanokouji learns about Karuizawa's past bullying and promises to shield her if she helps him, making her his most trusted pawn.

relationships.name: Kakeru Ryuen
relationships.detail: The Class C leader becomes obsessed with unmasking Class D's hidden mastermind and goes after Karuizawa to find him.

fights.title: Buying the old exam
fights.summary: Ayanokouji spends 15,000 points on a past test from an upperclassman, quietly saving Sudo and the class from failing.

fights.title: Winning the island exam
fights.summary: By letting Ibuki steal Horikita's leader card and taking over as leader himself, he tricks Class A and Class C into guessing wrong.

fights.title: The cruise VIP exam
fights.summary: Ayanokouji watches Karuizawa get cornered by Class C girls, then offers her protection if she will cooperate with him on the exam.

fights.title: Ayanokouji vs. Ryuen
fights.summary: Ayanokouji walks onto the rooftop, admits he is the mastermind, and overpowers Ryuen and his group.

keyEpisodes.why: Debut as a seemingly average new student in Class D.
Chabashira reveals that his father wants him expelled, and Ayanokouji vows to defy him.
He meets his father face to face at the school and refuses to leave.
His identity as the mastermind is exposed to Ryuen.

strength.rank: Class D's hidden mastermind and strongest fighter
strength.summary: Shaped by a harsh upbringing in the White Room, Ayanokouji hides both his intellect and his physical skill behind a bored front. When Ryuen corners Karuizawa on the rooftop, he easily takes down Ishizaki, Albert and the martial artist Ibuki, then beats Ryuen until he finally feels fear.

qualities.detail: When the starving pirate Gin is thrown out of the Baratie with no money, Sanji quietly brings him a hot meal anyway. Nobody who is truly hungry gets turned away by him.
He fights only with kicks, keeping his hands safe for the kitchen. Being a cook comes before being a fighter.
He swoons over every woman he meets and refuses to hurt one, a rule he keeps even when it nearly gets him killed.
While waiting tables he openly snubs the Marine lieutenant Fullbody, and when the officer wastes the food served to him, Sanji beats him up. Throwing away a meal is the one thing he won't tolerate.
He owes Zeff his life and stubbornly refuses to leave the Baratie, even as it's attacked. When he finally sails off, he drops to his knees in tears to thank the old man.

sanji.backstory: Sanji was born a prince of the Germa Kingdom, a floating nation run by his father, Vinsmoke Judge, who experimented on his children to make them stronger and emotionless. Their mother Sora secretly took a drug to undo the changes, and only Sanji was affected: he grew up with ordinary strength and real feelings. Judge called him a failure and locked him away while his brothers bullied him, until his sister Reiju helped him escape, and Judge ordered him never to reveal he was a Vinsmoke. Working as a young kitchen hand on a passenger ship, he was swept overboard when the pirate 'Red Foot' Zeff attacked. Stranded together on a rock, Zeff gave the boy all their food. After their rescue, the pair built the floating restaurant Baratie, where Zeff trained Sanji as a cook and in kick-based fighting. Both dreamed of finding the All Blue.

journey.summary: He meets Luffy, defends the restaurant from Don Krieg's pirates and finally accepts that he can leave Zeff to chase his own dream. He joins the Straw Hats as their cook.
He fights Fish-Men to free Nami's village, then, in Arabasta, poses as 'Mr. Prince' to lure Crocodile away and help the crew escape a trap.
He tracks Robin onto the sea train to the judicial island, refuses to strike the CP9 agent Kalifa because she is a woman, and beats Jabra with his new Diable Jambe.
He offers his own life to Bartholomew Kuma in exchange for Luffy's. During the two-year separation he trains in the Kamabakka Kingdom and learns Sky Walk.

Forced into a political marriage with Big Mom's daughter Pudding, he leaves the crew to protect them and even fights Luffy to push him away. In the end he admits he wants to come back and helps save both the crew and his family.
In Wano he destroys his family's Raid Suit rather than become like his brothers, then defeats Queen. On Egghead he protects Nami and Bonney from powerful foes as the crew faces the Navy.

lessons.lesson: Hunger isn't something to punish.
lessons.why: Sanji feeds Gin, an enemy pirate, because he remembers starving on a rock with Zeff. Kindness learned in hard times gets passed on.

lessons.lesson: Gratitude can hold you back if you never let yourself go.
lessons.why: Sanji nearly stays at the Baratie forever out of debt to Zeff. Leaving with Luffy is how he honours their shared dream.

lessons.lesson: Your worth isn't what your family says it is.
lessons.why: Judge called him a failure, but the qualities his father hated, his compassion and his feelings, are what make Sanji a hero.

lessons.lesson: It's okay to ask for help.
lessons.why: On Whole Cake Island he tries to handle everything alone. Only when he admits to Luffy that he wants to stay with the crew can his friends help him save everyone.

relationships.name: Zeff
relationships.detail: The former pirate who saved young Sanji at sea, gave up his own food (and his leg) so the boy could survive, then raised him as a cook at the Baratie.

relationships.name: Monkey D. Luffy
relationships.detail: Luffy keeps insisting that Sanji join as the crew's cook until Sanji finally leaves the Baratie with him.

relationships.name: Roronoa Zoro
relationships.detail: The two share a long-running rivalry and argue constantly, yet they are among the crew's three strongest fighters.

relationships.name: Nami
relationships.detail: Sanji showers Nami with compliments and special dishes, and the women of the crew are the people he most fiercely protects.

relationships.name: Vinsmoke Judge
relationships.detail: The king of the Germa Kingdom, who did nothing while Sanji's brothers abused him as a child and later threatens Zeff to make Sanji obey and accept an arranged marriage.

relationships.name: Vinsmoke Reiju
relationships.detail: The one Vinsmoke sibling who showed him kindness, helping him escape the kingdom to pursue his dream of cooking.

relationships.name: Charlotte Pudding
relationships.detail: Big Mom's daughter is set to marry Sanji to tie Germa to the Big Mom Pirates; despite his attraction to her, he refuses to go through with it.

fights.title: Sanji vs. Pearl
fights.summary: When Don Krieg's men attack the Baratie, Sanji reveals his kicking style against the armored Pearl.

fights.title: Sanji vs. Kuroobi
fights.summary: At Arlong Park, Sanji struggles against the fish-man underwater, then beats him once the fight moves onto land.

fights.title: Sanji vs. Mr. 2 Bon Clay
fights.summary: Mr. 2 copies Nami's face to stop Sanji attacking, but Sanji figures out the ballet-fighter must change back to strike and wins.

fights.title: Sanji vs. Jabra
fights.summary: In Enies Lobby, Sanji overcomes Jabra's iron-body martial arts with his new flaming Diable Jambe kicks.

fights.title: Sanji vs. Absalom
fights.summary: Furious at Absalom's plan to force Nami into a wedding, Sanji fights the invisible man at Thriller Bark.

fights.title: Sanji vs. Queen
fights.summary: On Onigashima, Sanji discovers Ifrit Jambe and blasts Queen right off the island.

keyEpisodes.why: Debut as the hot-tempered sous-chef of the Baratie.
He leaves the Baratie and Zeff to sail with Luffy as the crew's cook.
Sanji clashes with his father Judge as his royal past comes out.
He knocks Luffy down and walks away, while Luffy vows to wait for him to come back.
His victory over Queen marks his rejection of the Germa legacy.

strength.rank: One of the Straw Hats' top three fighters
strength.summary: Sanji fights only with his legs to protect his cook's hands, and is counted with Luffy and Zoro among the crew's 'Monster Trio'. He beat the CP9 agent Jabra with his new Diable Jambe, and in Wano his awakened Germa enhancements and Ifrit Jambe let him defeat the Beast Pirates All-Star Queen.

qualities.detail: She knows one spell and refuses to learn a second. Every skill point she earns goes into making Explosion bigger, even when a party would happily take a mage with ordinary fire or ice magic.
Like most Crimson Demons she introduces herself with a pose and a grand speech, wears an eyepatch purely for effect and treats a daily blast like a stage performance.
Mock her name, her clan or her spell and she will demand an apology on the spot, and she is not above threatening to blow up the offender's house.
Behind the act she has the highest Intelligence in Kazuma's party and is often the one who notices what the others have missed.
She turns up to join Kazuma's party so starved she collapses, and she makes no secret that regular meals are part of the appeal.

megumin.backstory: Megumin grew up in the Crimson Demon village, a settlement of red-eyed mages, in a family so poor that she often foraged for her own food and looked after her little sister Komekko. As a small child she disturbed something sealed near the village and was rescued by a mysterious woman who wiped out the monster with Explosion. Megumin begged to be taught; the woman warned her off, and her teachers at the village academy dismissed the spell as a useless novelty. She saved her skill points anyway, sparring constantly with her classmate and self-declared rival Yunyun. When demons attacked while she was searching for Komekko, she found she finally had enough points, learned Explosion and destroyed the horde. She adopted a strange black cat, Chomusuke, graduated and set off to find the woman who saved her, only to be turned away by party after party until she reached Axel.

journey.summary: She answers Kazuma's recruitment notice half-starved, wipes out a toad with Explosion and immediately collapses. Kazuma keeps her, partly to avoid a scene in the guild, and starts carrying her home after her daily blast.

Her daily target practice on an abandoned castle provokes the castle's owner, Verdia, a general serving the Devil King. She later blows away his undead army, and against the Mobile Fortress Destroyer she casts twice in one day after Kazuma drains magic from Aqua into her.

Yunyun follows her to Axel to keep their rivalry going. At Darkness's own request Megumin casts Explosion on her to destroy Vanir's possessing mask, and at the Arcanletia hot springs she and Wiz bring the general Hans down to size.

Fearing for her home, she takes the party to her birthplace, which the general Sylvia keeps raiding. When Sylvia returns as a giant fused monster, Megumin and Yunyun take in the villagers' magic through Wiz and destroy her, with Kazuma caught in the blast and later revived.

She helps destroy a lake hydra, sabotages Kazuma's search for a replacement tank, and presses him to act when Darkness agrees to a forced marriage. In the finale she threatens to blow up the town if Alderp's men touch Darkness.

After the battle against Wolbach in the capital, she confesses her feelings to Kazuma and they settle into something they describe as sitting between friendship and romance. She is alive at the end of the main series. The anime has not adapted this part as of November 2026.

lessons.lesson: Specialising has a price, and you should know what it is.
lessons.why: Megumin chose one spell knowing she would be useless after casting it. Party after party rejected her before Kazuma, and she never pretends the trade-off is free.

lessons.lesson: The people who carry you matter.
lessons.why: Every Explosion ends with Megumin face down in the dirt. Kazuma hauling her home each day becomes the quiet base of their friendship.

lessons.lesson: Rivals can be the friends who know you best.
lessons.why: Yunyun mocks Explosion for years, yet in the prequel she drops her own plans to save Komekko, and in Legend of Crimson the two cast the finishing blow together.

lessons.lesson: Real support means backing someone's dream, not editing it.
lessons.why: At the end of Legend of Crimson Megumin asks Kazuma to spend her points on practical magic. He puts them into Explosion instead, and her next blast is the strongest yet.

relationships.name: Kazuma Satou
relationships.detail: The first adventurer willing to keep her despite the one-spell limit; he carries her after every cast and becomes her partner on daily explosion walks.

relationships.name: Yunyun
relationships.detail: The Crimson Demon chief's daughter, who keeps challenging Megumin to duels and is quietly the closest friend she has outside the party.

relationships.name: Aqua
relationships.detail: The goddess whose huge magic reserve gets funnelled into Megumin through Kazuma's Drain Touch when one Explosion isn't enough.

relationships.name: Darkness
relationships.detail: The party's Crusader and shield. Megumin treats her like family and nearly levels a street to keep her out of a forced marriage.

relationships.name: Komekko
relationships.detail: The little sister Megumin raised in their struggling household; saving her in the prequel is what finally gets Megumin her spell.

relationships.name: Wiz
relationships.detail: The lich shopkeeper is one of the few other people who can cast Explosion, and the two team up against the Destroyer and Hans.

relationships.name: Chomusuke
relationships.detail: The small black cat she named and keeps at home is actually part of the sealed Dark God Wolbach, which demons keep coming to reclaim.

strength.rank: One-shot artillery mage
strength.summary: Explosion is the most destructive attack spell in the KonoSuba world, and Megumin pours every point she earns into making it stronger. One cast wipes out a general's undead army or the legs of a walking fortress, but it drains her completely, so she can fire once a day and then has to be carried home.

fights.title: Wiping out Verdia's undead army
fights.summary: Once Kazuma and Aqua lure Verdia's undead knights clear of the town, Megumin erases the whole army with a single Explosion.

fights.title: Stopping the Destroyer
fights.summary: She and Wiz blast the legs off the charging fortress; refilled with Aqua's magic, she casts a second time to finish it before it self-destructs.

fights.title: Blowing up Vanir
fights.summary: With Vanir's mask stuck on Darkness's face, Darkness tells Megumin to hit her with Explosion; the demon is destroyed and Darkness walks away.

fights.title: First Explosion in the Crimson Demon village
fights.summary: Cornered by demons while protecting Komekko and Yunyun, she discovers she has enough points, recites her rescuer's chant and destroys the horde.

fights.title: Megumin and Yunyun vs. Sylvia
fights.summary: Charged with the whole village's magic, the two rivals combine their spells to destroy the giant revived Sylvia.

fights.title: Draining the lake hydra
fights.summary: After adventurers sap the hydra's mana, Megumin finishes the regenerating beast with Explosion.

keyEpisodes.why: Her pompous introduction, her one-spell confession and her first collapse in front of Kazuma.
Kazuma starts joining her daily Explosion outings at the abandoned castle, which brings Verdia to Axel's gate.
Her two Explosions in one day are the key to bringing down the Destroyer.
The prequel shows the young Megumin being saved by a stranger's Explosion and resolving to learn it.
Legend of Crimson takes her home, gives her the finishing blow, and ends with Kazuma backing her dream.
She stands up to Alderp's guards with a threat to blast the town, protecting Darkness.

qualities.detail: Rules from APE and the adults barely register with her. When she is ordered away from Plantation 13, she disobeys and climbs into Strelizia with Hiro anyway.
She calls Hiro 'darling' from their first meeting, smothers his breakfast in honey and treats the other pilots' discomfort as entertainment.
Feared as a monster because of her horns and klaxosaur blood, she stays apart from the squad and admits she has never really belonged anywhere.
She wants to become fully human, and for much of the series believes that killing enough klaxosaurs is the way to earn it.
Her nickname, the Partner Killer, comes from the fact that no co-pilot had lasted beyond three rides with her before Hiro.

zero-two.backstory: Zero Two was created in a laboratory by Dr. Franxx, who used genetic material from the Klaxosaur Princess to make a human-klaxosaur hybrid. As a child in the Garden she had red skin, long horns and no words, and researchers subjected her to painful tests of her regenerative powers. The one thing that comforted her was a storybook, The Beast and the Prince. A boy coded 016, who would later be called Hiro, saw how she was treated, smashed a window to free her and fled with her. They were caught, his memories of her were wiped, and she kept their time together as a promise to become human so she could find him again. She later served with the Nines under the code Nine Iota before becoming an elite special-forces pilot whose co-pilots kept dying.

journey.summary: Hiro finds her swimming near Plantation 13 and, when her partner is mortally wounded, climbs into Strelizia with her. After a disastrous ride with Mitsuru, she is ordered to leave; Hiro begs her to stay, and they survive his feared third ride together.

Assigned permanently to the squad, she slowly loosens up, yet her horns and fangs keep growing. At the Garden she ignores orders and charges klaxosaurs alone, desperate to kill enough of them to become human.

A deep link reveals that Hiro is the boy from her childhood. Ashamed of having used him as fodder, she lashes out at the squad and leaves for the Nines, until Hiro reaches her in Strelizia, tells her he loves her and the two break into the Gran Crevasse.

She learns she was cloned from the Klaxosaur Princess. When the princess seizes Strelizia, Zero Two fights her way back to Hiro, and together with the princess they turn the Star Entity against the invading VIRM, leaving Zero Two's body unresponsive.

Her mind is fighting VIRM above Mars inside Strelizia Apus. Hiro joins her there, they become Strelizia True Apus and travel for two years to the VIRM homeworld, where they sacrifice themselves to destroy it. Centuries later they are shown reborn as two children who find each other.

lessons.lesson: Being called a monster doesn't make you one.
lessons.why: Zero Two half-believes the label until Hiro remembers her. Her cruellest moments come when she is most convinced she is only a beast.

lessons.lesson: You can't earn love by keeping score.
lessons.why: She tries to buy her humanity with a klaxosaur body count, and only finds it when she stops counting and lets Hiro see what she is.

lessons.lesson: Partnership means sharing the cost.
lessons.why: Every earlier co-pilot was used up. Hiro survives because he chooses to ride with her knowing the risk, and they start carrying the load together.

relationships.name: Hiro
relationships.detail: A washed-out pilot who becomes the only co-pilot to survive Strelizia with her. They turn out to be the two children who once escaped the Garden together.

relationships.name: Ichigo
relationships.detail: Squad 13's leader distrusts Zero Two for endangering Hiro and clashes with her repeatedly over Hiro's health.

relationships.name: Mitsuru
relationships.detail: Wanting to prove himself better than Hiro, he rides Strelizia with her once and comes back badly hurt and shaken.

relationships.name: Dr. Franxx
relationships.detail: The scientist who designed the Franxx made Zero Two from the Klaxosaur Princess's DNA and oversaw her childhood experiments.

relationships.name: Nine Alpha
relationships.detail: Leader of the Nines, the elite unit where she served as Nine Iota; in the final battle he helps Hiro reach her and dies in the fight.

relationships.name: Klaxosaur Princess
relationships.detail: The ancient klaxosaur leader whose DNA Zero Two was cloned from; she hijacks Strelizia before the two of them unite to save Hiro.

relationships.name: Kokoro
relationships.detail: When Zero Two's body is left behind on Earth, the pregnant Kokoro refuses to leave her side even through a storm.

strength.rank: Elite special-forces pilot
strength.summary: Part human and part klaxosaur, Zero Two has greater strength and fast healing, and she can operate Strelizia with far more power than an ordinary pistil. On her first sortie with Hiro the transformed Strelizia beats the attacking klaxosaur almost effortlessly, and other pilots repeat rumours that she can drive a Franxx without any partner at all.

fights.title: First ride with Hiro
fights.summary: With her partner dying, Zero Two takes Hiro aboard; Strelizia shifts into its true form and crushes the klaxosaur attacking Plantation 13.

fights.title: Defying orders at the transport
fights.summary: As she is being escorted away, a klaxosaur strikes; she ignores her orders and pilots with Hiro, who keeps control this time.

fights.title: The Gutenberg-class klaxosaur
fights.summary: During the joint defence with Plantation 26, Strelizia's first strike fails; Hiro recovers to fight beside her and the squads bring the giant down.

fights.title: Breaking into the Gran Crevasse
fights.summary: Nearly lost to her own rage, she reconnects with Hiro mid-battle and Strelizia destroys the Super-Lehmann klaxosaur by itself.

fights.title: Strelizia Apus against VIRM
fights.summary: With the Klaxosaur Princess, she restores the dying Hiro and seizes the Star Entity, which becomes Strelizia Apus and drives off VIRM.

fights.title: The VIRM homeworld
fights.summary: After two years of travel, she and Hiro reconnect through their friends' prayers and give their lives to destroy VIRM's planet.

keyEpisodes.why: She meets Hiro at the lake and takes him into Strelizia.
Hiro asks her to stay, and she chooses him over her orders.
Her childhood in the Garden and her escape with young Hiro are revealed.
Hiro reaches her and the two reconcile in Strelizia.
She sacrifices her consciousness to save Hiro and stop VIRM.
The finale: her last mission with Hiro and their reincarnation.

qualities.detail: He races Kageyama to the gym every morning, keeps a running tally of who wins, and is usually the last one still asking for more practice.
Shorter than nearly every blocker he faces, he answers the problem with speed and an enormous jump rather than accepting that volleyball is for tall people.
His first reaction to meeting Shiratorizawa's ace Ushijima, a player far above his level, is to challenge him on the spot.
Before his only middle-school tournament match he is so anxious he bolts for the bathroom, yet he still walks out insisting his team can win.
Coach Ukai quickly sees him as the ultimate decoy: Hinata gladly draws the blockers so that teammates can score.

shouyou-hinata.backstory: As a small boy Shouyou Hinata stopped his bike in front of an electronics shop where a television showed Karasuno High playing at the national Spring tournament. Their ace, a short player people called the Small Giant, was beating blockers much taller than him, and Hinata decided he would do the same. At Yukigaoka Junior High he was the only member of the boys' volleyball club, so he practised alone in corners of the gym and hallways for two years. In his third year a few first-years joined, and he borrowed friends from the basketball and soccer clubs to make up a team for one official tournament. Their first opponent was Kitagawa Daiichi, home of the gifted setter Tobio Kageyama, and Yukigaoka was beaten badly. Hinata walked away vowing to beat Kageyama and headed for Karasuno.

journey.summary: He finds Kageyama on the same team and the two are barred from the club until they win a three-on-three match. Their eyes-closed quick attack, in which Kageyama places the ball into Hinata's swing, becomes Karasuno's main weapon.
Wearing the number 10 his idol once wore, he works as the team's decoy against Date Tech's Iron Wall, but Aoba Johsai blocks his final spike in a 33–31 loss that ends their tournament.
Wanting to control the ball in mid-air, he clashes with Kageyama until they rebuild the quick together. Karasuno beats Aoba Johsai to reach the Miyagi final.
Ushijima mocks his style as clumsy. Hinata answers with running blocks and a key spike, and Karasuno wins the fifth set to qualify for nationals.

journey.stage: Nationals (To the Top and The Dumpster Battle)
journey.summary: After his ball-boy stint at the youth camp, he plays at Tokyo's national tournament, where Karasuno beats Inarizaki and then Nekoma, finally getting the official match against Kenma he had wanted since their first meeting.

Mid-match against Kamomedai he collapses with a 39.1°C fever, is taken off and watches Karasuno's loss from hospital. After graduating he trains in beach volleyball in Brazil, then joins the MSBY Black Jackals in Japan's top league, faces Kageyama's Schweiden Adlers and later signs with Asas São Paulo. The anime had not adapted this part as of November 2026.

lessons.lesson: A weakness can be a starting point.
lessons.why: Hinata could not out-reach tall blockers, so he built a game on speed, timing and leaping, the qualities that made his idol great.

lessons.lesson: Doing the unglamorous job still counts.
lessons.why: Shut out of a youth camp, he worked as a ball boy and came back a far better receiver, which pays off in the Inarizaki match.

lessons.lesson: Taking care of yourself is part of competing.
lessons.why: His fever against Kamomedai cost him the match he most wanted. Coach Ukai's point that the body is a player's foundation reshapes how he trains afterwards.

lessons.lesson: Rivals push you further than friends who agree.
lessons.why: Kageyama's refusal to change the quick, and their fight over it, led to the improved attack that carried Karasuno to nationals.

relationships.detail: The setter who beat him in middle school becomes the other half of the freak quick; the two compete at everything, even who reaches the gym first.

relationships.name: Kenma Kozume
relationships.detail: Nekoma's quiet setter meets Hinata by chance on a jog, and Hinata keeps trying to make volleyball exciting enough for Kenma to care about winning.

relationships.name: Kei Tsukishima

relationships.name: Wakatoshi Ushijima

relationships.name: Tooru Oikawa

relationships.name: Natsu Hinata

fights.title: Loss to Aoba Johsai

Their quick attack finally clicks, turning two rivals into partners.
Hinata's wish to fly on his own terms sparks a bitter argument with Kageyama.
Karasuno beats Shiratorizawa and earns a trip to nationals.
Left out of the youth camp, he sneaks in and ends up as a ball boy.
The win over Inarizaki shows how far his all-round game has come.

qualities.detail: She sees every Angel as a chance to prove she is Nerv's best pilot and treats Shinji's successes as a personal insult.
She calls Shinji an idiot within minutes of meeting him and mocks Rei's obedience to the commander without bothering to lower her voice.
Unlike Shinji, she has prepared for piloting most of her life and already holds a university degree from Germany when she arrives in Japan.
Her bragging is aimed at adults she wants approval from, above all Kaji, whom she follows around and tries to impress.
Each defeat chips away at her, and her synchronisation with Unit-02 falls as her confidence goes.

asuka-langley.backstory: Asuka grew up in Germany as the daughter of Kyoko Zeppelin Soryu, a scientist on the Evangelion project. An experiment with Unit-02 left Kyoko mentally broken and hospitalised; she stopped recognising her daughter and talked to a doll as if it were Asuka. When Asuka was chosen as Unit-02's pilot, she ran to tell her mother, hoping the news would win back her attention, and found that Kyoko had hanged herself. Her father soon remarried, and Asuka never felt close to her stepmother. She decided she would stand on her own, never cry, and prove her worth by being the best. She trained relentlessly, finished university early and was placed in the care of Ryoji Kaji, who escorts her and Unit-02 to Japan on a United Nations fleet in 2015.

journey.summary: She meets Shinji aboard the UN carrier, drags him into Unit-02's cockpit and kills the sea Angel Gaghiel. Soon living in Misato's flat, she and Shinji train to move in perfect step and defeat the split Angel Israfel.

She captures, then has to fight, the Angel Sandalphon inside a volcano and is saved by Shinji when her lifeline snaps. Her rivalry with Shinji grows more tangled, including an awkward kiss in their apartment.

As Shinji's sync ratio passes hers, her performance slips. The Angel Arael forces her to relive her mother's death, Unit-02 shuts down, and Rei has to finish the Angel. Asuka spirals into depression, runs away and is found catatonic by Nerv agents.

Placed inside Unit-02 during the attack on Nerv, she realises her mother's soul has been in the Eva all along. She destroys the invading soldiers and beats the nine Mass Production Evangelions until her power runs out; they revive and tear Unit-02 apart.
After Third Impact she is lying beside Shinji on the beach of a sea of LCL, bandaged but alive. When he begins to strangle her, she touches his face, and the film ends on her flat reaction to him.
The Rebuild films reimagine her as Asuka Shikinami Langley, a different take on the character with a new backstory and her own ending.

lessons.lesson: Never needing anyone is a wall, not a strength.
lessons.why: Asuka built her identity on never relying on others. When she finally needs help after Arael, she has pushed everyone away.

lessons.lesson: A worth that depends on winning will not survive losing.
lessons.why: Her confidence and her sync ratio rise and fall with each Angel. One defeat after another is enough to bring both down.

lessons.lesson: Old wounds return until they're faced.
lessons.why: Arael breaks her by replaying the memory she had tried hardest to bury: finding her mother after the suicide.

relationships.name: Shinji Ikari
relationships.detail: Her rival and reluctant partner; she taunts him constantly, yet they defeat Israfel together and he dives into a volcano to save her.

relationships.name: Rei Ayanami
relationships.detail: Asuka scorns Rei's silence and calls her the commander's obedient doll.

relationships.name: Ryoji Kaji
relationships.detail: Her escort from Germany, whose attention she craves; he treats her affection with gentle distance.

relationships.name: Misato Katsuragi
relationships.detail: Nerv's operations director takes Asuka into her apartment alongside Shinji and plans their battles.

relationships.name: Kyoko Zeppelin Soryu
relationships.detail: The scientist whose breakdown and suicide shaped Asuka's personality; part of her soul is later found within Unit-02.

relationships.name: Hikari Horaki
relationships.detail: Shinji's class representative becomes Asuka's closest friend at school and sets her up on a blind date.

strength.rank: Nerv's most thoroughly trained pilot
strength.summary: Asuka has trained for Eva combat since childhood and pilots Unit-02 with aggressive, acrobatic precision. On her first sortie she fights the sea Angel Gaghiel from a ship's deck, and in the 1997 film she defeats armed soldiers and all nine Mass Production Evas before her power runs out.

fights.title: Unit-02 vs. Gaghiel
fights.summary: She leaps from ship to ship with Shinji in her cockpit; dragged underwater, the pair pry the Angel's jaws open so two sunken battleships can fire into it.

fights.title: The dance against Israfel
fights.summary: After days of practice in step with Shinji, the two Evas strike both halves of the Angel at the same instant.

fights.title: Magma dive against Sandalphon
fights.summary: The Angel wakes while she is retrieving it from a volcano; she kills it deep in the magma and nearly sinks before Shinji catches her.

fights.title: Broken by Arael
fights.summary: The orbiting Angel's light invades her mind and replays her childhood trauma until Unit-02 stops responding.

fights.title: Unit-02 vs. the Mass Production Evangelions
fights.summary: Reconnected with her mother, she wrecks the JSSDF assault and downs all nine white Evas before her battery dies and they rise again.

keyEpisodes.why: Her loud arrival on the UN fleet and her first Angel kill.
She moves in with Shinji and Misato, and their joint attack defeats Israfel.
Her backstory is revealed as Arael breaks her will.
She is found catatonic after running away.
Her last stand in Unit-02 and her place in the final scene.

qualities.detail: Between bounties he lies around the Bebop, complains about dinners of bell peppers with no beef, and shrugs at danger with his line 'Whatever happens, happens.'
Once a fight starts he is a different man: fluid in hand-to-hand combat, quick with a pistol and reckless in his fighter, the Swordfish II.
He refuses to explain his history with the Red Dragon Syndicate to Jet, yet drops everything the moment he hears a rumour about Julia.
He grumbles constantly about Faye, Ed and Ein joining the ship, but he lets a bounty escape so he can catch a falling corgi with his ship.
He tells a fortune-teller that a woman has already killed him once, and he acts like a man with very little left to lose.

spike-spiegel.backstory: Spike was born on Mars and drifted into crime, eventually finding a home in the Red Dragon Syndicate under its leader Mao Yenrai. He rose fast, became a partner and friend of the ruthless Vicious, and was talked about as a possible future leader. An accident on a syndicate job cost him an eye, which was replaced with an artificial one. After he was wounded in a gunfight, Julia, who was Vicious's girlfriend, cared for him while he recovered, and the two fell in love. They planned to run away together. Vicious learned of it and told Julia she must kill Spike or die with him. Spike faked his death to get out of the syndicate, but Julia never came to their meeting place, choosing to hide rather than betray him. Spike later partnered with Jet Black, a former police officer, as a bounty hunter.

journey.stage: Bounty hunting on the Bebop (early sessions)
journey.summary: Spike and Jet chase small bounties across the solar system and rarely get paid. Along the way the ship picks up Ein, a data dog, Faye Valentine, a gambler drowning in debt, and the teenage hacker Ed.
Hearing that Vicious has killed a syndicate boss, Spike goes after him alone. He is beaten in an old cathedral and thrown through a window, surviving with Faye at his side.
A rumour that Julia is on Callisto sends him off the Bebop. He finds Vicious instead, is shot by his former subordinate Lin with a tranquiliser, and learns from Gren that Julia is alive and hiding.
He survives the near-invulnerable assassin Mad Pierrot at an amusement park, wins a duel against the would-be cowboy Andy, and watches Ed and Faye each leave the ship in search of their own pasts.

Vicious seizes the Red Dragon and his assassins hunt Spike. Spike is finally reunited with Julia, but she is shot and dies in his arms. He says goodbye to Jet and Faye, storms the syndicate's tower and kills Vicious, then walks down the stairs, points a finger-gun at the gunmen, says 'Bang' and collapses. Director Shinichiro Watanabe has never confirmed whether he dies.

Set between sessions 22 and 23, the film has the crew hunting Vincent Volaju, a former soldier who releases deadly nanomachines in Mars's capital, with Spike working alongside the agent Electra after first clashing with her.

lessons.lesson: You can't outrun the past by pretending it's over.
lessons.why: Spike treats his syndicate years as a closed book, yet one mention of Julia or Vicious pulls him back every time.

lessons.lesson: The people around you are part of your life, even if you never admit it.
lessons.why: Jet and Faye want him to stay, and Faye begs him not to go. He returns to the Bebop for one last meal with Jet before he leaves.

lessons.lesson: Living as if you're already dead has a cost.
lessons.why: Spike talks as though his life ended when he left the syndicate. That lets him take any risk, but it also keeps him from the future Jet and Faye are offering.

relationships.name: Faye Valentine

relationships.name: Edward Wong Hau Pepelu Tivrusky IV

relationships.name: Ein
relationships.detail: The corgi Spike rescues while chasing a pet thief, and the dog proves to be an unusually intelligent data dog.

relationships.name: Mao Yenrai
relationships.detail: The Red Dragon boss who took Spike under his wing; Vicious kills him, which draws Spike back into the syndicate's affairs.

strength.rank: Former Red Dragon enforcer turned bounty hunter
strength.summary: Spike follows Bruce Lee's Jeet Kune Do philosophy in hand-to-hand combat, handles a pistol with precision and flies the Swordfish II with daredevil skill. He has a talent for walking away from injuries that should have killed him, such as his fall through the cathedral window in his first clash with Vicious.

fights.title: Chasing Asimov
fights.summary: Spike tangles with a drug-boosted bounty head, survives a beating and pursues his ship to a police blockade.

fights.title: Showdown in the cathedral

fights.title: Snow on Callisto

fights.title: Mad Pierrot

fights.title: Final duel with Vicious
fights.summary: After shooting his way up the syndicate tower, Spike and Vicious trade weapons in a standoff; Spike shoots him in the chest but is badly cut.

First look at Vicious and Spike's buried syndicate past.
Flashbacks to Julia and to working alongside Vicious, and the news that she is alive.
The syndicate comes for Spike and Julia reaches out through Faye.
Julia's death, Spike's farewell and his final duel.

qualities.detail: Still powerless, he sprints into a villain attack to pull Bakugo free simply because he could not stand there and watch, which is exactly what convinces All Might.
He has filled notebooks with notes on every hero and Quirk he sees, and mutters his analysis aloud in a way that unnerves his classmates.
Early on he would rather shatter his own bones with One For All than leave someone in danger, as he does when he punches a giant robot during the entrance exam.
He cries easily, from relief, frustration or gratitude, and the series treats that openness as a strength rather than a weakness.
Unable to control his power in the first battle trial, he punches upward through the building so Ochaco can reach the target and win.

izuku-midoriya.backstory: Izuku Midoriya grew up in a world where most people develop a superpower, a Quirk, by the age of four. He never did. His mother, Inko, raised him largely on her own while his father worked abroad, and his childhood friend Katsuki Bakugo, whose Quirk produces explosions, turned into his tormentor, nicknaming him Deku, a word suggesting someone useless. Izuku still worshipped All Might, the hero who stood for peace itself, rewatching his rescue videos and filling notebooks with hero analysis. At fourteen he finally met his idol, who told him a Quirkless boy should be realistic and become a police officer instead. Minutes later the same sludge villain grabbed Bakugo, and Izuku charged in with no power at all. Moved, All Might revealed his secret: his Quirk, One For All, can be passed on, and he wanted Izuku to inherit it.

journey.summary: After ten months of punishing training under All Might, he swallows a strand of his hair to receive One For All. In the entrance exam he scores no combat points but smashes a giant robot to save Ochaco Uraraka, earning enough rescue points to pass.
He pushes Shoto Todoroki to use his fire side even though it costs him the match, then learns the Full Cowl technique from Gran Torino and, with Iida and Todoroki, takes down the Hero Killer Stain.

He beats the villain Muscular to save the boy Kota, joins the effort to rescue the kidnapped Bakugo, and sees All Might's career end. A night-time fight with Bakugo finally lets them talk honestly about One For All.
Using Eri's Rewind Quirk, he fights Overhaul at 100 percent without breaking his body. Later he learns that One For All carries the Quirks and spirits of its past holders, starting with Blackwhip.

After the war in Jaku City, he writes letters to his class revealing One For All's secret and leaves U.A. to hunt villains alone. Worn down to a ragged state, he is dragged back by Class 1-A, and Ochaco persuades frightened evacuees to let him rest inside the school.

journey.stage: Final War and epilogue (Season 7 and Final Season)
journey.summary: He transfers parts of One For All into Shigaraki to break All For One's hold, reaches the boy Tenko inside, and with the past holders destroys All For One. Left with only the embers of the Quirk, he loses it entirely by graduation. Eight years later he teaches at U.A., until All Might presents him with a powered suit built so he can return to hero work.

lessons.lesson: Courage comes before power.
lessons.why: All Might picks Izuku not for any talent, but because he ran toward danger when every hero with a Quirk held back.

lessons.lesson: Saving people includes letting them save you.
lessons.why: When Izuku tries to carry the war alone, his classmates repeat his own words back to him: helping without being asked is what heroes do.

lessons.lesson: Understanding an enemy can end a fight better than beating them.
lessons.why: In the final battle Izuku reaches Tenko's memories and finds the scared child inside the villain, which leads to All For One's defeat.

lessons.lesson: Losing a power doesn't erase the hero.
lessons.why: Quirkless again in the epilogue, he keeps teaching and helping until he can return to the field in a suit his friends paid to build.

relationships.name: All Might
relationships.detail: The Symbol of Peace trains him and passes on One For All, then becomes his teacher at U.A.

relationships.name: Katsuki Bakugou
relationships.detail: The boy who bullied him as 'Deku' becomes his fiercest classmate and, eventually, one of the friends who fights at his side.

relationships.name: Ochaco Uraraka

relationships.name: Shouto Todoroki
relationships.detail: Izuku's challenge at the Sports Festival helps Todoroki start accepting the fire side he inherited from his father.

relationships.name: Tenya Iida

relationships.name: Tomura Shigaraki

relationships.name: Inko Midoriya
relationships.detail: She raises him mostly alone, sews his first hero costume from his own sketch and fears for him every time he is hurt.

relationships.name: Eri
relationships.detail: A girl held by Overhaul whose Rewind Quirk lets Izuku fight at full power; he later helps her learn to smile again.

strength.rank: Ninth holder of One For All
strength.summary: One For All stockpiles the strength of everyone who has held it, and at first a single punch shatters Izuku's arm. His first punch in the entrance exam flattens a giant robot but wrecks his arm and legs, so the early story is about learning to control a power his body cannot yet handle without breaking.

fights.title: Deku vs. Kacchan
fights.summary: In a hero-versus-villain drill he holds off an enraged Bakugo and smashes upward through the building so Ochaco can secure the target.

fights.title: Sports Festival vs. Todoroki
fights.summary: He breaks his fingers flicking away ice and goads Todoroki into using his flames, then loses the match.

fights.title: Stopping the Hero Killer
fights.summary: With Iida and Todoroki in a Hosu back alley, he helps overpower Stain, and both he and Iida end up badly hurt.

fights.title: Saving Kota from Muscular
fights.summary: Beaten badly, he throws everything into one huge punch to drive the villain into the ground.

fights.title: Infinite 100% vs. Overhaul

fights.title: The final blow on All For One
fights.summary: Cheered on by his class and the whole country, he runs through All For One's attacks and, together with Shigaraki and the past holders, ends him.

keyEpisodes.why: He rushes to save Bakugo without a Quirk, and All Might chooses him.
The entrance exam, where his first use of One For All saves Ochaco.
His second fight with Bakugo clears the air between them.
He leaves letters for his class and walks out of U.A.
Class 1-A brings him home.
The series finale and its look eight years ahead.

ages.when: Start of the series (meeting All Might)

qualities.detail: He keeps fixed working hours, dresses like an office worker and makes it plain that he would rather clock out than do one minute of unpaid overtime.
He tells Yuji frankly that he does not yet accept him as a sorcerer, but also that children should not have to carry adult burdens, and he acts on it.
He states his low opinion of Gojo openly, and his praise for Yuji, when it finally comes, is plain and sincere.
He teaches Yuji to read cursed-energy residue and explains his own technique mid-fight, treating each case like a careful investigation.
Discovering that Mahito's victims are transformed humans still in pain, he turns cold and focused on ending the curse responsible.

jujutsu-kaisen-kento-nanami.backstory: Kento Nanami went through Tokyo Jujutsu High as a junior to Gojo and Geto. His classmate and close friend Yu Haibara, a cheerful boy who admired their seniors, was killed on a mission that turned out far more dangerous than it was rated, and Nanami was left standing over his body in the morgue. After graduating, he decided sorcery was not worth it and took a corporate job, only to find it hollow work that cared about nothing but money. Four years later he exorcised a small curse that had been bothering a worker at a bakery he visited, and her simple thanks reminded him that this kind of work mattered. He returned to jujutsu, rose to Grade 1, and approaches it with the habits of the office: fixed hours, neat suits and as little drama as possible.

journey.summary: Gojo hands Yuji over to him while he investigates a series of deaths at a cinema. Nanami teaches him to track cursed residue and discovers that the 'curses' they are fighting were once human.

In the sewers he takes Mahito apart once his working hours end and his overtime vow kicks in, but the curse escapes. Later he and Yuji corner Mahito together; trapped in Mahito's domain, Nanami thinks he is about to die until Yuji breaks in.
As a student he loses Haibara on a mission rated far below its real danger, one of the events that drive Geto away from jujutsu society.
He rescues the wounded Ijichi, beats the curse user Haruta for attacking Megumi and Yuji, and joins Maki and Naobito against Dagon. Jogo then burns all three, leaving Nanami horribly injured.

Barely conscious, he cuts through a crowd of transfigured humans while dreaming of a quiet beach in Malaysia. Mahito reaches him in front of Yuji and kills him; his last words hand the fight over to Yuji. In the manga he later appears in Yuji's thoughts and in Gojo's afterlife scene.

lessons.lesson: Burnout is not a moral failure.
lessons.why: Nanami left jujutsu after losing Haibara and came back on his own terms. The series treats both choices as legitimate.

lessons.lesson: Meaning can come from small thanks.
lessons.why: What brought him back wasn't a grand cause, just a bakery worker grateful he had lifted a curse she couldn't see.

lessons.lesson: Adults owe children protection, not just training.
lessons.why: He refuses to let Yuji fight alone, takes the worst of Mahito on himself, and only at the very end entrusts the rest to him.

lessons.lesson: Boundaries are a form of strength.
lessons.why: His overtime vow turns his dislike of extra hours into real power, a reminder that limits can be chosen deliberately.

relationships.name: Yuji Itadori
relationships.detail: Assigned to watch over Yuji, he goes from refusing to recognise him as a sorcerer to trusting him as a colleague.

relationships.name: Satoru Gojo

relationships.name: Mahito
relationships.detail: The curse that turns people into monsters is the first enemy Nanami fights beside Yuji, and the one who finally kills him.

relationships.name: Yu Haibara
