relationships.name: Takuma Ino
relationships.detail: A younger sorcerer who works with Nanami in the sewers and again in Shibuya.

relationships.name: Jogo
relationships.detail: The volcanic curse who burns Nanami, Maki and Naobito in Shibuya, leaving Nanami fatally injured.

strength.rank: Grade 1 jujutsu sorcerer
strength.summary: His Ratio Technique marks a weak point at the 7:3 line of any target, and a self-imposed binding vow means his cursed energy surges once he passes his set working hours. In the sewers that is enough to break Mahito's arm and take him apart until the curse reshapes his own soul to flee.

fights.title: Lesson in the cinema district
fights.summary: Nanami and Yuji each take on a curse; Nanami demonstrates his Ratio Technique and stops Yuji before he kills a creature that was once human.

fights.title: Overtime against Mahito
fights.summary: When his working hours end, Nanami unleashes his full strength and catches Mahito off guard in the sewers.

fights.title: Nanami and Yuji vs. Mahito
fights.summary: The pair pressure Mahito until he traps Nanami in his domain; Yuji forces his way in and the curse has to flee.

fights.title: Punishing Haruta
fights.summary: Finding the curse user about to kill Yuji and Megumi, Nanami beats him down in a rare display of anger.

fights.title: Dagon's domain
fights.summary: With Maki and Naobito he survives a swarm of shikigami inside the curse's domain until Toji Fushiguro appears.

fights.title: Last stand in Shibuya Station
fights.summary: Badly burned, he fights off transfigured humans until Mahito kills him in front of Yuji.

keyEpisodes.why: He begins working with Yuji and sets out his view of jujutsu as a job.
Facing death, he recalls the bakery that brought him back to sorcery.
Haibara's death, the loss that shaped his student years.
Jogo burns him, Maki and Naobito.
His death and his last words to Yuji.

qualities.detail: She heads straight for Harajuku on arrival and is delighted to hear the class is going to Roppongi, until she learns it is for a mission rather than sightseeing.
During the Kyoto event she rejects the idea that a woman sorcerer has to be pretty or meek, insisting she will decide her own worth.
She pins a curse with a nail through its own severed arm and, after learning the Death Painting brothers were part human, says she does not regret exorcising them.
She bickers with Yuji constantly, yet is furious that he hid his survival from her and Megumi for weeks.
Her reason for leaving her village is partly a promise to herself to find Saori, an older girl the locals drove away.

jujutsu-kaisen-nobara-kugisaki.backstory: Nobara grew up in a small rural village, raised by her grandmother, a scarred sorcerer who taught her the Straw Doll Technique. As a young girl she befriended a classmate named Fumi, and the two idolised Saori, a girl from Tokyo whose family had moved to the village. The villagers shunned Saori's family as outsiders until they left. Disgusted by that narrow-mindedness, Nobara decided she would get out and go to Tokyo too, hoping to see Saori again. By the end of middle school she was already working as a sorcerer under her grandmother, and after an argument with her, she won her place at Tokyo Jujutsu High. Arriving by train from Morioka, she meets Gojo in Harajuku along with Yuji Itadori and Megumi Fushiguro, the two other members of the year.

journey.summary: Gojo sends her and Yuji into an abandoned Roppongi building as a test, where she freezes when a curse takes a child hostage, then uses Resonance on the curse's severed arm to finish it after Yuji intervenes.

A special-grade curse overwhelms the group at the detention centre and Yuji appears to die. She trains with the second-years, bonds with Maki, and is angry to discover later that Yuji's death was kept secret from her.
She fights Momo Nishimiya and comes close to winning before Mai Zen'in's revolver shot puts her out of the event.
Infected with the Rot technique alongside Yuji, she turns Resonance on the brothers Eso and Kechizu, and the two first-years defeat them.

She returns to the fight after getting Akari to safety, hits Mahito's soul with Resonance through his double, and is then touched by the real Mahito. After smiling and telling Yuji that her life 'wasn't so bad', her face is blasted open; Arata Nitta's treatment leaves a slim chance she is alive.

In chapter 253 she reappears, missing an eye, and strikes Sukuna's last hidden finger with Resonance, stunning him so Yuji can land the final blow. She survives the series and reunites with her estranged mother and her grandmother. The anime had not reached this as of November 2026.

lessons.lesson: You get to decide who you are.
lessons.why: Nobara rejects both her village's idea of a proper girl and the jujutsu world's sexist expectations, as she says openly during the Kyoto event.

lessons.lesson: Leaving a toxic place can be an act of loyalty.
lessons.why: Her move to Tokyo is a rejection of the village that drove Saori away, and a way of keeping faith with a friend.

lessons.lesson: Teamwork isn't the opposite of independence.
lessons.why: Proud as she is, her biggest wins come in partnership: with Yuji against Eso and Kechizu, and with Yuji's final strike against Sukuna.

relationships.name: Yuji Itadori
relationships.detail: Her partner in fights and arguments alike; they finish the Death Painting brothers together.

relationships.name: Megumi Fushiguro
relationships.detail: The quieter third member of the trio, who drags her out of danger at the detention centre.

relationships.name: Satoru Gojo
relationships.detail: Gojo recruits her as the third first-year and leads the trio's earliest missions.

relationships.name: Maki Zen'in
relationships.detail: The second-year who fights without cursed energy; Nobara trains with her and throws Maki's name back at her sneering twin, Mai.

relationships.name: Momo Nishimiya
relationships.detail: The Kyoto third-year she battles at the Goodwill Event over their clashing views on women in jujutsu.

relationships.name: Saori
relationships.detail: The city girl her village drove out; the memory pushes Nobara toward Tokyo.

relationships.name: Mahito
relationships.detail: The curse who uses Nobara to hurt Yuji, striking her face with Idle Transfiguration in Shibuya.

strength.rank: Grade 3 first-year sorcerer
strength.summary: The Straw Doll Technique lets her drive cursed energy through nails with a hammer. With Resonance she can hit a target remotely by nailing a straw doll through something taken from it, as she does with a curse's severed arm on her first mission, and her nails can be detonated on impact.

fights.title: The curse in the abandoned building
fights.summary: After Yuji frees the hostage child, she uses Resonance on the curse's cut-off arm to exorcise it.

fights.title: Nobara vs. Momo Nishimiya
fights.summary: She is close to beating the broom-riding Kyoto student before Mai's revolver takes her out.

fights.title: Yuji and Nobara vs. Eso and Kechizu
fights.summary: As the brothers' rot technique eats at them, her Resonance turns the fight and the pair exorcise the Death Paintings.

fights.title: Mahito's double in Shibuya
fights.summary: Her Resonance damages both Mahitos at once, but a swap through a corridor lets the real one reach her.

keyEpisodes.why: Her arrival in Tokyo, her first mission and a look at the friend who shaped her.
Her fight with Momo and her speech on being a woman sorcerer.
She and Yuji defeat Eso and Kechizu and face what killing a half-human curse means.
Her memories of home and her farewell to Yuji.
Arata Nitta says there is still a slim chance she survives.

qualities.detail: He talks a military court into handing Eren to the Survey Corps and, at the recruitment ceremony, convinces new cadets to join a branch where most soldiers die.
He hides the real goal of the 57th expedition even from his own officers, dangling Eren in front of the enemy to expose a spy, at the cost of many soldiers.
Whether facing mockery, arrest or a Titan's jaws, he keeps the same steady expression and keeps giving orders.
Behind his speeches about humanity sits a personal goal: proving the theory about the walls that got his father killed.
He designed the long-range scouting formation that lets the Corps spot Titans early and steer around them.

erwin-smith.backstory: As a boy, Erwin wondered why nobody remembered anything from before humanity moved behind the walls. His father, a schoolteacher, privately suggested that the king had altered people's memories to control them. Erwin repeated the theory to other children, and soon afterwards his father died in an 'accident' arranged by the Military Police's Interior Squad. Carrying that guilt, Erwin enlisted, befriended fellow trainee Nile Dawk, and entered the Survey Corps. There he stopped talking about the theory and admitted privately that he fought for answers rather than for humanity. He proved an outstanding soldier, devised the long-range scouting formation while still a squad leader, and eventually succeeded Keith Shadis as the thirteenth commander. Along the way he pulled the thief Levi out of the Underground and into the Corps.

journey.summary: With Levi he visits the imprisoned Eren and argues at his trial that the Survey Corps should control him. He then tells new cadets the next expedition aims at the Yeager family basement.
Secretly using Eren to lure out the spy among them, he traps the Female Titan in the forest, but she escapes. He later plans the capture of Annie in Stohess and is arrested for the damage.
He leads the charge to rescue Eren from Reiner and Bertolt, driving Titans into the Armored Titan; a Titan bites off his right arm, yet he keeps ordering the advance.
Framed and sentenced to death, he reveals his father's fate and, with Pyxis and Zackly, carries out a bloodless coup that puts Historia on the throne.

Pinned down by the Beast Titan's barrage, he confesses to Levi how badly he wants to see the basement, then leads the recruits in a suicide charge so Levi can reach Zeke. Mortally wounded, he is brought back, and Levi chooses to give the serum to Armin and lets him die.

lessons.lesson: Leaders must own their costs.
lessons.why: Erwin never pretends his plans are clean; he accepts arrest after Stohess and says plainly that his soldiers' deaths must be given meaning.

lessons.lesson: Personal motives don't cancel public good.
lessons.why: He fought mostly to prove his father right, yet his choices kept humanity alive. The series lets both be true.

lessons.lesson: Knowing when to stop is its own courage.
lessons.why: On the roof at Shiganshina he admits his dream to Levi, then gives it up to lead the charge that wins the battle.

relationships.name: Levi
relationships.detail: Erwin recruited Levi from the Underground, and Levi follows him above anyone, while also being the one person who can speak to him bluntly.

relationships.name: Eren Yeager
relationships.detail: Erwin secures custody of the Titan-shifter and builds his plans around Eren and the basement in his old home.

relationships.name: Hange Zoë
relationships.detail: The Corps' Titan researcher and one of Erwin's senior officers, who succeeds him as the 14th commander.

relationships.name: Nile Dawk
relationships.detail: His fellow trainee became commander of the Military Police, and the two clash and cooperate across the series.

relationships.name: Armin Arlert
relationships.detail: Erwin values Armin's insight; at Shiganshina Levi gives the one dose of serum to Armin instead of Erwin.

relationships.name: Keith Shadis
relationships.detail: The previous commander rejected Erwin's formation idea and later stood down, handing him the Survey Corps.

relationships.name: Zeke Yeager
relationships.detail: The Beast Titan whose rock barrage cuts down Erwin and his charging recruits.

strength.rank: 13th Commander of the Survey Corps
strength.summary: Erwin's real weapon is planning. He designed the formation that cut the Corps' losses outside the walls, and in the forest his ambush pins the Female Titan with hundreds of cables. Even after losing his right arm he insists on riding at the head of his troops.

fights.title: Trapping the Female Titan
fights.summary: Hidden squads launch a storm of cable-firing devices that pin her among the giant trees, though she later breaks free.

fights.title: The operation in Stohess
fights.summary: Erwin orchestrates the attempt to capture Annie inside the walls and faces Nile's gun when the plan turns into a battle.

fights.title: Rescuing Eren
fights.summary: He drives a horde of Titans into the Armored Titan; his arm is torn off as he shouts for the charge to continue.

fights.title: The suicide charge
fights.summary: Erwin rides at the head of the recruits into the Beast Titan's barrage and is struck down, buying Levi his chance.

keyEpisodes.why: Erwin and Levi stage the trial that wins the Corps custody of Eren.
His secret plan to unmask the spy is revealed.
He reveals that his father was killed for questioning the government.
His confession to Levi and the speech before the final charge.
Levi lets Erwin die and saves Armin.

qualities.detail: She holds herself to the standard of the Tohsaka name and is openly let down when the Servant she worked so long to summon is not what she hoped for.
She spends her family's most precious jewel to bring a dying classmate back to life, then insists she did it purely to settle her own conscience.
Showing Archer around the city, she admits she doesn't actually want anything from the Grail. She just intends to win.
Learning how carelessly Shirou has trained his magecraft, she is furious and immediately starts correcting him.
Brilliant at magecraft, she is notoriously helpless with modern electronics.

rin-tohsaka.backstory: Rin is the heir of the Tohsaka family, which helped create Fuyuki's Holy Grail Wars two centuries ago. As a little girl she idolised her father, Tokiomi, and in the war fought a decade before the story, while sent away for safety, she slipped back into the city alone to rescue a kidnapped school friend, using a magical compass and her own small magecraft to break a serial killer's hold over the captured children. Tokiomi never came home from that war. Before it began he had given her younger sister, Sakura, to the Matou family for adoption, a loss Rin carried quietly for years. The priest Kirei Kotomine, her father's student, became her guardian and handed her Tokiomi's ceremonial dagger at the funeral. Rin grew up to manage the family's dwindling fortune and its magecraft alone, preparing to enter the next war and win it in her father's name.

journey.summary: Rin summons Archer, is unimpressed by his attitude, burns a Command Seal on impulse to make him obey, and then shows him around the city. When she finds Shirou dying at school after Lancer's attack, she saves him with her father's jewel pendant.

She explains the war to Shirou, takes him to Kirei, and spares him the first night. After Berserker shows how outmatched they are, she and Shirou form an alliance against Caster, sharing her home and training him.
At Ryuudou Temple Archer abandons her for Caster. Shirou comforts her and confesses his feelings. She later learns Archer's true goal, forms a new contract with Saber, and is taken hostage by Archer.
Kirei reveals that he killed her father and intends to use her as the Grail's vessel; the dying Lancer turns on his Master and frees her.

She transfers her Magic Crest into Shirou so he can draw on her mana, then pulls Shinji out of the Grail. Archer's voice keeps her from giving up as Saber destroys it, and he says goodbye after asking her to look after Shirou.
Two years later she studies at the Clock Tower in London with Shirou as her apprentice and partner, vowing to stay by his side despite his ideals.

lessons.lesson: Rivals can still be allies.
lessons.why: Rin swears she will fight Shirou the next time they meet, then teams up with him as soon as the situation calls for it.

lessons.lesson: Self-sacrifice isn't the only form of heroism.
lessons.why: After Illya's death Rin tells Shirou he will break if he never values his own happiness, a challenge to his ideal of saving everyone.

lessons.lesson: Loss shouldn't stop you moving forward.
lessons.why: Betrayed by Archer and orphaned by Kirei, she keeps fighting, and in the end Archer's last words are about her future, not his regrets.

relationships.name: Archer
relationships.detail: A sardonic Heroic Spirit who treats her with grudging respect after she forces him into line with a Command Seal.

relationships.name: Shirou Emiya
relationships.detail: The classmate she saves with her pendant, then allies with and trains; in Unlimited Blade Works they become a couple.

relationships.name: Saber
relationships.detail: Shirou's Servant, who fights beside Rin and later forms a new contract with her after Archer's betrayal.

relationships.name: Kirei Kotomine
relationships.detail: Her father's former student and her legal guardian, whom she distrusts and who turns out to have killed Tokiomi.

relationships.name: Sakura Matou
relationships.detail: Given up for adoption to the Matou family as a child; Rin watches over her from a distance and feels guilty for years.

relationships.name: Tokiomi Tohsaka
relationships.detail: The previous head of the Tohsaka family, who never returned from the previous Grail War and left Rin his legacy.

relationships.name: Illyasviel von Einzbern
relationships.detail: Master of Berserker; Rin tries to take her out in the cemetery fight and barely escapes.

relationships.name: Lancer
relationships.detail: The Servant who nearly kills Shirou at the start later turns on Kirei to free Rin, dying as he does so.

strength.rank: Head of the Tohsaka family of mages
strength.summary: Rin stores magical energy in gemstones over years and spends them like ammunition, and fires Gandr, a cursing shot from her finger. In the opening nights she restores Shirou's destroyed heart with her pendant's stored power and attacks Illya directly in the middle of a Servant battle.

fights.title: Archer and Rin vs. Berserker
fights.summary: Their long-range support barely scratches Berserker, and Rin's attempt on Illya is turned back by bird-shaped homunculi.

fights.title: Ambush on Kuzuki
fights.summary: Rin fires a spell to test the suspected Master, then holds Caster's attention while Saber is overwhelmed by Kuzuki's fists.

fights.title: Rescuing Shinji from the Grail
fights.summary: Wading through the Grail's black mud at Ryuudou Temple, she drags Shinji out so it loses its vessel.

fights.title: Child Rin vs. the Fuyuki kidnapper
fights.summary: Sneaking into the city alone, the young Rin overloads Uryuu's bracelet with mana and frees the captured children.

keyEpisodes.why: The prologue tells the start of the war from Rin's side, ending with her saving Shirou.
She attacks Shirou, saves him from Rider and agrees to a truce.
Archer betrays her and Shirou confesses.
She shares her Magic Crest with Shirou, and he glimpses how she first noticed him.
The epilogue in London.
Kirei gives her Tokiomi's dagger after the funeral, relishing her grief.

qualities.detail: His school essay dismisses youth and friendship as a lie told by hypocrites, and his narration picks apart every social group he sees.
He quickly maps who leads Hayato's circle and why, and uses those insights to solve Service Club requests that defeat more popular students.
His solutions often work by making himself the villain, such as insulting the festival committee chair so she will come back and finish her job.
He dotes on his younger sister Komachi and readily agrees to anything she or his gentle classmate Saika asks.
When he learns Yui's friendliness may stem from the accident in which he saved her dog, he cuts her off rather than accept what he sees as charity.

hachiman-hikigaya.backstory: By the time Hachiman Hikigaya started high school, a string of embarrassing failures in middle school had taught him to expect rejection, and he hoped to begin again at Sobu High School, where nobody from his old school would know him. That plan collapsed on the first day: on his way to the entrance ceremony he dived in front of a car to save a dog and ended up in hospital for weeks, so by the time he arrived the class had formed its groups without him. He settled into life as a self-declared loner who eats lunch alone at his favourite spot outside and treats isolation as a principle. The dog, he later learns, belonged to his future classmate Yui Yuigahama, and the car belonged to the family of Yukino Yukinoshita.

journey.summary: Hiratsuka drafts him into the Service Club with the cold, brilliant Yukino Yukinoshita, and Yui soon joins. He helps with cookies, a tennis challenge and class group dynamics, then breaks off contact with Yui after learning about the dog.

journey.stage: Summer camp and the cultural festival (Season 1)
journey.summary: To free the isolated girl Rumi from her clique, he engineers a confrontation that splits the group. At the festival he takes the blame for the committee's failures and harshly confronts its chair, Minami, making himself hated across the school.
He fakes a confession to Hina to spare a classmate's doomed attempt, which wounds Yukino and Yui. When he and Yukino clash over Iroha's student council election, the club nearly falls apart.
Pushed by Hiratsuka, he admits his schemes caused the rift and, close to tears, tells Yukino and Yui he wants something genuine rather than polite distance.

journey.stage: The prom and the end of the club (Kan)
journey.summary: He backs Yukino's prom against her mother's opposition, even staging a decoy plan to make hers look better. On a bridge he finally tries to tell her what she means to him; after the prom she confesses, and the Service Club is revived with Yui's own request.

lessons.lesson: Taking all the blame isn't the same as solving the problem.
lessons.why: Hiratsuka praises his results but tells him it hurts to watch him sacrifice himself every time, and his Kyoto stunt nearly breaks the club.

lessons.lesson: Saying what you want is harder than fixing things for others.
lessons.why: His turning point is admitting, in his own clumsy words, that he wants something genuine with Yukino and Yui.

lessons.lesson: Kindness and guilt can look alike from the outside.
lessons.why: He pushes Yui away believing she only feels obliged; she tells him she would have befriended him even without the accident.

relationships.name: Yukino Yukinoshita
relationships.detail: His sharp-tongued equal; their clashing views on how to help people drive the club, and their bond becomes the centre of the series.

relationships.name: Yui Yuigahama
relationships.detail: The cheerful classmate whose dog he saved; she keeps reaching out to him and holds the club together.

relationships.name: Komachi Hikigaya
relationships.detail: The only person he admits to relying on; she drops hints about his life and pushes him toward his friends.

relationships.name: Shizuka Hiratsuka
relationships.detail: The teacher who forces him into the club and later points out the real cost of his self-sacrificing methods.

relationships.name: Saika Totsuka
relationships.detail: A gentle classmate from the tennis club, one of the few people whose invitations Hachiman never turns down.

relationships.name: Hayato Hayama
relationships.detail: The popular boy who tries to keep everyone happy; he and Hachiman respect and resent each other's methods.

relationships.name: Iroha Isshiki
relationships.detail: A first-year he persuades into becoming student council president, who then keeps dragging him into her projects.

fights.title: The tennis court showdown
fights.summary: After Yukino tires, Hachiman uses the sea breeze to lob two high serves that win the match against Hayato's group.

fights.title: Breaking Rumi's clique
fights.summary: His scheme pressures the girls shunning Rumi into turning on each other, weakening their hold on her.

fights.title: Finding Minami
fights.summary: He tracks the missing committee chair to a rooftop and needles her into returning, enraging Hayato in the process.

fights.title: The fake confession in Kyoto
fights.summary: To protect a friend group's balance, he cuts in front of Tobe and confesses to Hina himself, knowing she will refuse.

fights.title: Winning the election his way
fights.summary: He talks Iroha into wanting the presidency she was trying to avoid, sidestepping the rival plan Yukino had committed to.

keyEpisodes.why: His essay lands him in the Service Club with Yukino.
He learns Yui owned the dog he saved and pushes her away.
His festival stunt and Hiratsuka's warning about his self-sacrifice.
He asks Yukino and Yui for help and admits he wants something genuine.
His long conversation with Yukino on the bridge.
The prom, Yukino's confession and a new start for the club.

qualities.detail: She speaks to classmates in clipped sentences, refuses to explain herself and seems to treat friendship as a risk she cannot afford.
Every action she takes points at one goal: keeping Madoka Kaname from ever signing a contract with Kyubey.
She attacks Kyubey on sight in the very first episode and offers no explanation to the girls who see it.
She warns Mami about a witch before it strikes and talks about Walpurgisnacht weeks before it arrives, as if she has seen it all already.
From her first day she outshines the class in lessons and sport, which only makes her aloofness more unsettling.

akemi-homura.backstory: Homura was not always the girl Madoka meets. Originally she was a timid, bespectacled student with a heart condition that had kept her in hospital for months, and when she transferred into Madoka's class she had no confidence and no friends. Madoka befriended her, praised her name and, with Mami Tomoe, saved her from a witch, revealing that both were magical girls. When the enormous witch Walpurgisnacht killed Mami and then Madoka, Homura contracted with Kyubey, wishing to redo her meeting with Madoka and become the one who protects her instead. The wish gave her a shield that controls time and sent her back to her first day. Loop after loop, Madoka died or turned into a witch; in one, Homura had to break Madoka's Soul Gem at her own request. Shedding her glasses and braids, she began the next loop determined to rely on no one.

journey.summary: She appears in Madoka's dream, then in her classroom, warning her to stay as she is. She clashes with Mami over Kyubey and, after Mami is killed by the witch Charlotte, finishes the witch herself.

She tries to stop Madoka from contracting, ends a fight between Sayaka and Kyouko, and allies with Kyouko against the coming Walpurgisnacht. After Sayaka becomes a witch and Kyouko dies stopping her, Homura is left alone.
Earlier timelines show her shy beginnings, her wish, the discovery that magical girls become witches, and the promise she made to a dying Madoka.

She faces the witch alone with an arsenal of stolen weapons and is overwhelmed. Madoka makes her wish to erase witches throughout time, and Homura becomes the only person who remembers her in the rewritten world.

Trapped in a dream city inside her own Soul Gem while Kyubey studies her, Homura realises the truth and is nearly carried away by Madoka. Instead she seizes part of Madoka's power, becomes a self-described demon and rewrites the universe so Madoka can live as an ordinary girl again.

lessons.lesson: Love can harden into control.
lessons.why: Homura's devotion begins as gratitude and ends, in Rebellion, with her overriding Madoka's own choice.

lessons.lesson: Trying alone has limits.
lessons.why: Her vow to rely on no one makes her stronger, but she still falls to Walpurgisnacht by herself.

lessons.lesson: Every effort leaves traces.
lessons.why: Kyubey explains that her repeated resets have tied so many timelines to Madoka that they made Madoka powerful enough to become the worst witch of all.

relationships.name: Madoka Kaname
relationships.relation: the person she lives to protect
relationships.detail: The classmate who once befriended her; Homura repeats time over and over to save her.

relationships.name: Kyubey
relationships.detail: The creature who grants wishes in exchange for contracts; Homura attacks it on sight and keeps it away from Madoka.

relationships.name: Mami Tomoe
relationships.detail: The veteran who distrusts Homura and ties her up just before her own death; in an earlier timeline she was Homura's mentor.

relationships.name: Sayaka Miki
relationships.detail: Madoka's friend refuses Homura's help and blames her for Mami's death as her own despair grows.

relationships.name: Kyouko Sakura
relationships.detail: A veteran magical girl who agrees to fight Walpurgisnacht with Homura before dying to stop Sayaka's witch.

strength.rank: Time-manipulating magical girl
strength.summary: Homura's shield can stop time and holds a huge store of weapons, but has no attack of its own, so she fights with stolen guns and homemade explosives used while time is frozen. In the third episode she disposes of the witch that has just killed Mami within moments.

fights.title: Finishing Charlotte
fights.summary: Released from Mami's binding by Mami's death, Homura destroys the witch and takes its Grief Seed.

fights.title: Stopping Sayaka and Kyouko
fights.summary: She steps between the two magical girls, knocking Sayaka out and sending Kyouko away.

fights.title: Shooting Kyubey
fights.summary: As Kyubey pressures Madoka to wish, Homura guns him down; a replacement body appears and names her a traveller from another timeline.

fights.title: Alone against Walpurgisnacht
fights.summary: She throws everything she has at the giant witch during the storm and is beaten down.

fights.title: Defying the Law of Cycles
fights.summary: When Madoka comes to take her, Homura tears away part of her power and remakes reality.

keyEpisodes.why: Her eerie introduction and warning to Madoka.
Mami's death and Homura's quick kill of the witch.
Her original timeline and the reason behind everything she does.
She keeps Madoka's memory in the new world.
Rebellion turns her into the story's demon.

qualities.detail: He regards every human and curse as beneath him and is openly insulted that a teenager like Yuji can hold him back.
He laughs with Mahito while Yuji begs him to save Junpei, treating other people's suffering as entertainment.
Rather than simply rampage, he tricks Yuji into a binding vow that lets him take control for one minute when he says a single word.
He takes a strange interest in Megumi's potential and warns Mahito never to touch his vessel's soul again.
Even an enemy he has just destroyed can earn a word of praise from him if they fought with real conviction.

jujutsu-kaisen-sukuna.backstory: In the Heian era, jujutsu's golden age a millennium ago, Ryomen Sukuna was a human sorcerer whom no one could defeat. His monstrous body, which had two faces and four arms, led people to call him a demon, and the jujutsu world named him the King of Curses. According to the manga, he was born a twin and consumed his sibling in the womb, and grew up shunned before rising to kill sorcerer after sorcerer of that golden age. He took in Uraume, a child whose sleep froze everyone nearby, as a loyal servant. When he died, his remains survived as twenty fingers so steeped in cursed energy that they could not be destroyed, only sealed away. Those fingers, ranked as special-grade cursed objects, are still scattered across Japan in the present day.

journey.summary: Yuji swallows a finger to save his friends, and Sukuna wakes inside him but cannot keep control. Gojo subdues him easily and proposes that Yuji eat all twenty fingers so the curse can be executed with its host.

Released to fight a special-grade curse, he kills it, then tears out Yuji's heart to keep control and toys with Megumi. Yuji dies to stop him; Sukuna revives him only after a binding vow whose terms Yuji does not remember.
He mocks Yuji's grief over Junpei, but warns Mahito off the first time the curse touches his soul and badly wounds him the second time.

Jogo forces ten more fingers into the unconscious Yuji. Sukuna kills the Hasaba sisters, defeats Jogo in a battle that wrecks Shibuya, reunites with Uraume, and destroys Mahoraga with his domain Malevolent Shrine, killing vast numbers of people before returning control to Yuji.

He seizes Megumi's body, uses Megumi's sister's possessor to crush his spirit, and kills Gojo in their duel in chapter 236. Yuji and the remaining sorcerers fight him in Shinjuku until Nobara's Resonance on his last finger lets Yuji land a final blow; Sukuna rejects one last offer of mercy and fades away (chapter 268). The anime had not reached these events as of November 2026.

lessons.lesson: Read the fine print before you agree.
lessons.why: Desperate to live, Yuji comes back from death under a vow he cannot remember, and Sukuna later exploits it in the manga.

lessons.lesson: Power without connection is lonely.
lessons.why: In the final battle Yuji tries to show Sukuna his hometown and ordinary life. Sukuna refuses even then and fades rather than change.

lessons.lesson: The worst harm can come through the people you love.
lessons.why: Sukuna aims his cruelty at Yuji's friends rather than at Yuji, and the Shibuya devastation done with Yuji's hands nearly breaks him.

relationships.name: Yuji Itadori
relationships.detail: The boy who swallowed his finger and keeps control of their shared body, to Sukuna's lasting irritation.

relationships.name: Satoru Gojo
relationships.detail: The modern sorcerer Sukuna sees as worth fighting; Gojo subdues him casually on their first meeting.

relationships.name: Megumi Fushiguro
relationships.detail: Sukuna is fascinated by Megumi's untapped potential from their first fight, and that interest becomes something far darker.

relationships.name: Mahito
relationships.detail: Sukuna laughs alongside Mahito once, then punishes him severely for laying hands on his soul.

relationships.name: Jogo
relationships.detail: The volcanic curse wants Sukuna as leader of the curses; Sukuna kills him in Shibuya, then praises his strength.

relationships.name: Uraume
relationships.detail: A curse user who served him in the Heian era and is waiting for him in the present.

relationships.name: Nobara Kugisaki
relationships.detail: In the manga, her Resonance through his last finger is the strike that pins him for Yuji's finishing blow.

strength.rank: The King of Curses
strength.summary: Even with only one or two fingers' worth of power he regenerates Yuji's severed hand, kills a special-grade curse in moments and overwhelms Megumi. His invisible slashes cut through almost anything, and his domain, Malevolent Shrine, rains cuts over everything within a radius of well over a hundred metres.

fights.title: Tested by Gojo
fights.summary: Sukuna takes over Yuji's body as Gojo arrives, and the sorcerer knocks him back under Yuji's control.

fights.title: The detention centre curse
fights.summary: Released after Yuji loses a hand, he regrows it and kills the special-grade curse that had nearly killed the first-years.

fights.title: Sukuna vs. Megumi
fights.summary: Holding Yuji's heart hostage, he fights Megumi for sport and finds himself intrigued.

fights.title: Sukuna vs. Jogo
fights.summary: He toys with the volcano curse across Shibuya before burning him away with a flame technique he unveils by saying 'Open'.

fights.title: Sukuna vs. Mahoraga
fights.summary: To keep Megumi alive, he fights the summoned shikigami and opens Malevolent Shrine, levelling a large area of the city.

keyEpisodes.why: Yuji swallows the finger and the King of Curses wakes up.
His cruelty toward Megumi and the death of his vessel.
Inside his domain he talks Yuji into the 'Enchain' vow.
Jogo feeds Yuji ten fingers and Sukuna takes over in Shibuya.
Malevolent Shrine flattens Shibuya and Yuji sees what his body was used for.

qualities.detail: She answers in as few words as possible and often takes questions at face value, which leaves Shinji unsure whether she is cold or simply unused to people.
She follows Commander Gendo Ikari's orders without visible hesitation and is the only person he treats with something like warmth.
Her apartment is a bare, cluttered room with used bandages and rubbish lying around, and she sees nothing strange about living that way.
During Operation Yashima she places Unit-00 between the Angel's beam and Shinji without being asked twice, treating her own survival as secondary.
After Shinji tells her to smile when she doesn't know how to react, she begins, haltingly, to notice her own feelings.

rei-ayanami.backstory: Rei is not what she seems. Gendo Ikari created her as a clone grown from the remains of his wife, Yui, who vanished into Unit-01, combined with the soul of the being called Lilith. In 2010 he brought a small girl to Nerv and introduced her as the child of an acquaintance. That first Rei mocked Naoko Akagi, the scientist behind the MAGI supercomputers, by repeating Gendo's private insults about her, and Naoko strangled the child before taking her own life. Another body replaced her, carrying her memories forward. This second Rei became the First Child and pilot of Evangelion Unit-00. An activation test before Shinji's arrival went out of control and badly injured her; Gendo burned his hands pulling open her entry plug, and the glasses he wore that day became something she treasured.

journey.summary: Shinji first sees her wheeled out injured, which pushes him into Unit-01. Once healed, she pilots Unit-00 and shields him from Ramiel's beam during Operation Yashima, and he finds her crying with relief afterwards.
With Asuka's arrival she becomes one of three pilots. Asuka sneers at her as Gendo's doll, while Rei carries the Lance of Longinus down to Terminal Dogma and begins to wonder about her own feelings.

She stops Arael with the Lance after Asuka is broken. When Armisael fuses with Unit-00, she self-destructs the Eva to protect Shinji. A new Rei appears with no memory of him, and Ritsuko shows Shinji the tank of spare bodies before destroying them.

Gendo tries to use her to start Third Impact on his terms, but she turns away from him, joins with Lilith and puts the outcome of Instrumentality in Shinji's hands. When he chooses a world of separate people again, she lets the giant form collapse.
The Rebuild films revisit her through several different clones, including one who spends the fourth film learning everyday life in a village before her body gives out while Shinji watches.

lessons.lesson: Obedience isn't the same as having no will.
lessons.why: Rei follows Gendo for most of the series, then refuses him at the decisive moment of The End of Evangelion.

lessons.lesson: Small kindnesses can change a life.
lessons.why: Shinji's advice to smile is a tiny gesture, yet it starts Rei's slow realisation that she can feel something for someone.

lessons.lesson: Being replaceable isn't the same as being worthless.
lessons.why: Rei once says that if she dies she can be replaced. The new Rei after episode 23 lacks the bond Shinji built with her predecessor, which shows the person was never truly interchangeable.

relationships.name: Shinji Ikari
relationships.detail: His insistence on reaching her during Operation Yashima gives her one of the few warm moments she has had with anyone.

relationships.name: Gendo Ikari
relationships.detail: The only adult she trusts; he burned his hands pulling her from an overheated entry plug, and she treasures the glasses he wore that day.

relationships.name: Asuka Langley Souryuu
relationships.detail: Asuka mocks her passivity and openly resents her closeness to the commander.

relationships.name: Ritsuko Akagi
relationships.detail: Ritsuko maintains Rei and knows her secret; furious at Gendo, she shows Shinji the spare bodies and destroys them.

relationships.name: Yui Ikari
relationships.detail: Shinji's mother, absorbed by Unit-01, whose remains Gendo used to create Rei, which is why she resembles Yui.

relationships.name: Kaworu Nagisa
relationships.detail: The final Angel recognises Rei as being like him, a link to the beings at the heart of Nerv's secrets.

strength.rank: Unit-00's pilot and the First Child
strength.summary: Rei is Nerv's first designated pilot and the steadiest under fire. In Operation Yashima she holds a shield in front of Unit-01 against Ramiel's beam long enough for Shinji's second shot, and later she is the one Gendo trusts to throw the Lance of Longinus into orbit to destroy Arael.

fights.title: Shielding Unit-01 from Ramiel
fights.summary: When Shinji's first shot misses, Rei throws Unit-00 in front of the Angel's beam and holds until his second shot lands.

fights.title: Holding off Matarael
fights.summary: During a city-wide blackout, the three pilots move through ducts and work together to bring down an Angel dripping corrosive acid.

fights.title: The Lance against Arael
fights.summary: On Gendo's order she hurls the Lance of Longinus into orbit, destroying the Angel tormenting Asuka.

fights.title: Self-destructing Unit-00
fights.summary: With Armisael merging into her Eva and moving toward Shinji, she triggers Unit-00's self-destruct and dies in the explosion.

keyEpisodes.why: Shinji sees her injured on a stretcher and agrees to pilot in her place.
Shinji visits her bare apartment and learns why Gendo's broken glasses matter to her.
Operation Yashima and Shinji asking her to smile.
Flashbacks show Naoko Akagi killing the first Rei.
Her sacrifice, her replacement and the spare bodies in Terminal Dogma.
She rejects Gendo and decides who shapes Instrumentality.

qualities.detail: Polite, beautiful and gentle with children, he wins the trust of almost everyone he meets, which is exactly what makes him dangerous.
He rarely needs to pull a trigger himself; a few well-chosen words push people toward despair, murder or suicide.
When Tenma tells him he cannot simply go around killing, Johan calmly asks why not.
He tells Tenma outright that Liebert is not his real name, and almost nothing about where he came from can be pinned down.
The one person he claims to love is his sister Anna, and much of his plan revolves around her and the memories they share.

johan-liebert.backstory: Johan and his twin sister were born in Prague as products of a secret eugenics programme, and their mother kept them hidden, dressing them alike. When the scientists came to take one twin for experiments, she handed over the girl, and Johan never stopped asking himself whether she had meant to protect him or had mistaken one child for the other. His sister escaped and told him what she had seen, and Johan began to treat her memories as his own. The twins fled and were found cold and starving near the Czechoslovak border by an East German officer, General Wolf, who named the boy Johan after a character in a picture book. Johan was sent to the orphanage Kinderheim 511, where he incited a massacre among staff and children, and was then adopted by the Liebert family alongside his sister.

journey.summary: In 1986 the boy is brought to Eisler Memorial Hospital with a bullet in his head after his adoptive parents are found shot. Dr. Tenma defies his director to save him; soon afterwards the director and two senior doctors die of poisoned candy, and the twins vanish.

Years later Johan executes a criminal he once hired, in front of Tenma, and admits he poisoned the doctors as a favour. Framed for the killings, Tenma begins hunting him, while Johan reaches out to his sister, now living as Nina Fortner.

Posing as a student, he becomes reader and confidant to the wealthy, nearly blind Hans Georg Schuwald and engineers a takeover of his affairs. At a library ceremony Tenma and Nina each fail to shoot him, and a fire set by his accomplice causes chaos.

journey.stage: Prague and the Red Rose Mansion (episodes 44–67)
journey.summary: Disguised as a woman calling herself Anna, he manipulates a detective and a lost boy. He burns the Red Rose Mansion, and when Nina finally confronts him she realises he had taken her memories of the experiments and made them his own.

He sets the people of a small town against one another and demands that Tenma shoot him. Instead, a drunken villager shoots Johan in the head, and Tenma operates to save him a second time. Lying in a police hospital, he seems to speak to Tenma about his mother's choice, and then his bed is found empty.

lessons.lesson: Saving a life doesn't make you responsible for every choice that person makes, but it can feel that way.
lessons.why: Tenma's decision to operate on a child sets up the entire series, and his struggle with that guilt drives him across Europe.

lessons.lesson: A person without a name can still be shaped by one question.
lessons.why: Johan's cruelty traces back to not knowing whether his mother saved him or abandoned him, the question he raises again in the last episode.

lessons.lesson: Evil often wins by getting people to give up on themselves.
lessons.why: Johan's victims are usually pushed into despair rather than attacked, which is why Nina's forgiveness in Ruhenheim matters.

relationships.name: Kenzo Tenma
relationships.detail: The neurosurgeon who chose to operate on Johan over the town's mayor, and who later takes it on himself to stop him.

relationships.name: Anna Liebert
relationships.detail: Living as Nina Fortner with no memory of their past, she is the one person Johan claims to love.

relationships.name: Heinrich Lunge
relationships.detail: The BKA inspector long insists that Johan is just a fantasy of Tenma's until the evidence finally convinces him.

relationships.name: Wolfgang Grimmer
relationships.detail: A journalist shaped by the same orphanage, who helps Tenma trace Johan's past in Prague.

relationships.name: Eva Heinemann
relationships.detail: Tenma's former fiancée, the director's daughter, saw Johan on the night of a killing and becomes a target as a result.

relationships.name: Roberto
relationships.detail: A former Kinderheim 511 child who carries out murders on Johan's behalf until the end in Ruhenheim.

relationships.name: Franz Bonaparta
relationships.detail: The author of the picture book that gave Johan his name, and one of the men behind the experiments that produced the twins.

fights.title: The execution at the construction site
fights.summary: Johan shoots the criminal Junkers in front of Tenma and walks away, revealing himself as a killer.

fights.title: Fire at the library
fights.summary: Tenma aims at Johan during the book donation ceremony, hesitates and is disarmed, and the building is set alight.

fights.title: Nina's confrontation
fights.summary: Facing his sister in an abandoned building, he retells the Red Rose Mansion story until she realises the memories were hers.

fights.title: The end in Ruhenheim
fights.summary: He threatens a boy to force Tenma's hand, only to be shot in the head by the boy's drunken father.

keyEpisodes.why: Tenma's choice to operate on the wounded boy.
Johan's true nature is revealed to Tenma.
Nina remembers what Johan did to the Lieberts that night.
The truth about the Red Rose Mansion and whose memories they were.
His last talk with Tenma and the empty hospital bed.

qualities.detail: A single glare is enough to bring his rowdy squad to heel, and he greets the hopeful Asta with crushing magic pressure and threats.
He built the Black Bulls out of people no one else wanted, and at the entrance exam he takes Asta and Noelle when the other captains pass them over.

His motto is about breaking past your limits in the moment, and he drops subordinates into impossible situations, like throwing Asta into whirlpools he cannot swim through, expecting them to find a way.
He gambles away his wages, hates being disturbed on the toilet and treats official conferences as an inconvenience.
He senses opponents' movements through ki, a skill from his homeland that he passes on to Asta during their first serious battle together.

yami-sukehiro.backstory: Yami was born far from the Clover Kingdom, in a distant eastern country, into a clan of sword-wielding assassins. As a boy he shielded his little sister, Ichika, from a violent father. When his father plotted a coup and prepared a drug to unlock Yami's power, Ichika took it instead and slaughtered the household; Yami took the blame and fled by boat. He washed up in the Clover Kingdom, unable to speak the language and scorned as a foreigner with dark magic. Julius Novachrono, then a squad captain, recruited him into the Grey Deer, taught him the language and gave him a place to belong, and Yami grew close to William Vangeance and to Nacht Faust, whose twin brother Morgen died in their squad. Once Yami became a captain himself, he founded the Black Bulls to give outcasts like himself somewhere to belong.

journey.summary: At the Magic Knights entrance exam, no captain wants the boy with no magic. Yami tests Asta's nerve by threatening him, then laughs and accepts him, followed by Noelle Silva.

journey.stage: Licht and the Eye of the Midnight Sun
journey.summary: He arrives through Finral's portal to save Asta, duels Licht, and teaches Asta to sense ki mid-fight. At the Underwater Temple he cuts through a barrier with his new Dimension Slash and kills Vetto.

After Julius appears to die, Yami fights the possessed Charlotte and cuts her spell in half to save the city. Against the devil behind the elves' massacre, he aims a long-range Dimension Slash: Equinox purely by ki and splits the creature.

Six months later, Dante of the Dark Triad attacks the Black Bulls' base to seize him. Yami creates Death Thrust, admits he needs Asta, and the two defeat Dante together before Zenon carries Yami off to the Spade Kingdom. This is where the original TV anime ends.

Sealed alongside Vangeance as a key to the underworld, he is freed when Asta cuts through Lucifero's manifestation with Yami's katana. Badly drained, he fights again in the war with Lucifero and later against Lucius's forces, where he faces the revived Morgen and is helped by Nacht and Ichika.

lessons.lesson: A team of misfits can outwork a team of elites.
lessons.why: The Black Bulls start the series with negative stars and climb to the top through stubbornness, largely because Yami gives outcasts a place to belong.

lessons.lesson: Strength includes asking for help.
lessons.why: Against the regenerating Dante, the squad's strongest fighter finally admits he can't win alone and fights beside Asta as an equal.

lessons.lesson: Your past doesn't have to define your home.
lessons.why: Yami arrived as a shipwrecked foreigner nobody trusted; Julius's acceptance became the model for how he treats his own recruits.

relationships.name: Asta
relationships.detail: Yami takes the magicless boy when no one else will, teaches him ki, and later fights beside him as an equal.

relationships.name: Noelle Silva
relationships.detail: A royal outcast he recruits alongside Asta and pushes to control her immense water magic.

relationships.name: Julius Novachrono
relationships.detail: The man who recruited the young foreigner, taught him the language and later entrusted the kingdom's future to him.

relationships.name: William Vangeance
relationships.detail: His Grey Deer partner who became captain of the Golden Dawn; Yami once suspected him of being Licht.

relationships.name: Charlotte Roselei
relationships.detail: The Blue Rose captain is in love with Yami, who once helped break her curse and is too oblivious to notice her feelings.

relationships.name: Vanessa Enoteca
relationships.detail: A witch whose cage Yami broke almost by accident before telling her to decide her own fate.

relationships.name: Nacht Faust
relationships.detail: His teenage friend and the first recruit of the Black Bulls, who later leads the plan to rescue him.

relationships.name: Ichika
relationships.detail: The sister he protected in his homeland, and whose bloody rampage he took the blame for when he fled.

strength.rank: Captain of the Black Bulls
strength.summary: Yami coats his katana in Dark Magic and cuts with enough force to overwhelm opponents, while using reinforcement magic to make up for his darkness's slow speed. His ki sense lets him read attacks before they land, and with a single glare he can cow every rowdy member of his squad at once.

fights.title: Testing Asta at the exam
fights.summary: Yami unleashes his magic pressure to frighten Asta, who stands his ground and earns a place in the Black Bulls.

fights.title: Yami vs. Licht
fights.summary: Light Magic meets Dark Magic in a cave as Yami blocks Licht's attacks by sensing his ki.

fights.title: Cutting through to Vetto
fights.summary: Yami slices through Abari's barrier with Dark Cloaked Dimension Slash and uses it again to finish Vetto.

fights.title: Equinox against the Word Soul devil
fights.summary: With his last magic, Yami aims his biggest Dimension Slash by ki alone and slices the devil apart.

fights.title: Yami and Asta vs. Dante
fights.summary: Yami condenses his Mana Zone into Death Thrust, then fights alongside Asta when Dante regenerates.

fights.title: Passing the katana
fights.summary: In the final seconds, Yami throws Asta his sword, and Asta's anti-magic slash defeats Dante before Zenon takes Yami.

Yami remembers being shunned until Julius took him in.
The story of his early days with Vangeance and the founding of the Black Bulls.
He gives Secre a Black Bulls robe in front of the Magic Parliament.
Yami is captured by the Dark Triad.

qualities.detail: He answers gossip, threats and supernatural events in the same dry tone, and rarely lets anyone see him rattled.
To kill a rumour about Tomoe, he embarrasses himself in front of the whole station platform rather than let her reputation suffer.
Whether it is a bunny girl nobody else can see or a junior trapped in a time loop, he gets involved as soon as he notices someone struggling.
He arranges his life around Kaede, who barely leaves their apartment, and helps her tick off a list of small goals one at a time.
A false story that he sent three classmates to hospital follows him everywhere, and he simply doesn't bother correcting it.

sakuta-azusagawa.backstory: Two years before the story begins, Sakuta's younger sister Kaede was bullied online, and cuts and bruises began appearing on her body. One morning she woke with no memory of her past. Their mother broke down under the strain, and the day after witnessing that, Sakuta woke with three deep gashes across his chest and ended up in hospital; doctors didn't believe his account and the rumour of a violent incident followed him. He threw his phone into the sea to cut himself off from the online world that had hurt Kaede. Around that time he met a high school girl on the beach, Shoko Makinohara, whose advice he still carries with him, and he fell for her. He now lives alone with Kaede in Fujisawa and attends Minegahara High School, still without a phone.

journey.summary: He spots Mai Sakurajima in the library in a bunny costume no one else notices, and realises people are forgetting her. Fighting sleep to keep remembering her, he forgets anyway, then remembers and shouts his love for her across the schoolyard, restoring her place in everyone's memory.
Trapped in a repeating day with Tomoe Koga, he agrees to a fake relationship to protect her from social fallout, then escapes a second loop by gently turning down her real feelings.
He helps his friend Rio Futaba accept the second version of herself, and talks Mai's half-sister Nodoka out of the sea after their body swap.
He helps Kaede achieve her goals one by one, but when her old memories return, the Kaede he spent two years with is gone, and he breaks down at the hospital.

journey.stage: A Dreaming Girl and the later films
journey.summary: Sakuta learns that in another future he is killed on the road and his donated heart keeps Shoko alive. Mai pushes him clear of the car and dies instead, and Shoko changes the past so no one dies. Later films follow Kaede back to school and his mother's recovery.

Now at a Yokohama university, he helps an idol classmate find her way back onto the stage at her group's concert, an old classmate split between realities and a student who reads minds, while chasing the mysterious 'Touko Kirishima'. Protecting Mai from an overcrowded stage, he is hurt and briefly hospitalised.

lessons.lesson: Noticing someone is the first way to help them.
lessons.why: Mai's syndrome makes her invisible, and Sakuta saves her simply by refusing to stop seeing her.

lessons.lesson: Being misunderstood isn't a reason to stop being kind.
lessons.why: Sakuta lives with an ugly rumour about himself, yet keeps stepping in for people whom everyone else overlooks.

lessons.lesson: Grief and gratitude can arrive together.
lessons.why: When the original Kaede returns, Sakuta mourns the sister he had for two years even while celebrating that she is back.

relationships.name: Mai Sakurajima
relationships.detail: The actress he alone could see in the library; after he brings her back, they become a couple.

relationships.name: Kaede Azusagawa
relationships.detail: The sister he protects and lives with; her memory loss is the root of his own scars.

relationships.name: Shoko Makinohara
relationships.detail: The girl on the beach who comforted him during his worst days; a younger Shoko later turns up with an illness of her own.

relationships.name: Rio Futaba
relationships.detail: The science club member who explains each syndrome in physics terms and keeps calling him a rascal.

relationships.name: Tomoe Koga
relationships.detail: A first-year whose fear of social rejection traps them both in a repeating day.

relationships.name: Yuma Kunimi
relationships.detail: One of the few classmates who never believed the rumours about Sakuta.

relationships.name: Nodoka Toyohama
relationships.detail: An idol who swaps bodies with Mai; Sakuta stops her from walking into the sea.

fights.title: Shouting across the schoolyard
fights.summary: After forgetting and then remembering Mai, he yells his confession for the whole school to hear, pulling her back into everyone's awareness.

fights.title: Facing Maezawa at the station
fights.summary: Taunted into a scuffle, Sakuta defuses the rumours about Tomoe by humiliating himself and her accuser instead.

fights.title: Breaking Tomoe's loop
fights.summary: Stuck repeating 18 July, he takes Tomoe to Enoshima and kindly refuses her confession to end the loop.

fights.title: Search in the rain for Rio
fights.summary: He runs through a storm to find the second Rio and collapses with a fever after reaching her.

fights.title: The car accident
fights.summary: Sakuta moves to save Shoko and Mai pushes him clear, forcing him to find a way to undo that day.

fights.title: The crowded stage in Fujisawa
fights.summary: When people convinced they are Touko Kirishima rush the stage, he shields Mai and is taken to hospital.

keyEpisodes.why: He meets Mai in the library.
His confession saves Mai from being forgotten.
Sakuta explains Kaede's past and his scars.
He mourns the Kaede he lost as the old one returns.
The truth about Shoko and the future he was never meant to survive.
University life begins with a new set of Adolescence Syndrome cases.

qualities.detail: On his first day back he steals Koro-sensei's gelato, leaves a dead octopus on his desk and treats the whole assassination job as a game of pranks.
He can match the school's top student, yet early on coasts into exams on talent and loses to Gakushu Asano because he barely studied.
In the class's internal battle over whether to kill Koro-sensei, his strategies give the 'kill' side an early lead.
After a teacher he trusted betrayed him, he arrives at Class 3-E ready to despise any adult who calls himself a teacher.
He calmly squares up to a professional assassin who has just punched through a window, and outplays him with his own weapon.

karma-akabane.backstory: Karma grew up in a wealthy household; his parents, financial day traders, were rarely home. At Kunugigaoka Junior High he ranked near the top academically and grew close to Nagisa Shiota in their first year. Later he stepped in to save a Class 3-E student being bullied by a top-ranked senior and badly hurt the bully. His homeroom teacher, who had seemed to be on his side, turned against him to protect his own reputation, leaving Karma convinced that teachers only care about themselves. Suspended for violent behaviour, he was assigned to Class 3-E, the school's dumping ground, where the Ministry of Defence briefed him on his new classmates' mission: kill their tentacled teacher before he destroys the Earth.

journey.summary: Returning from suspension, he becomes the first student to wound Koro-sensei by shaking his hand with knife fragments taped to his palm. After a day of failed tricks, he jumps from a cliff, gambling that his teacher will either save him or fail as a teacher; Koro-sensei catches him and Karma accepts him.
Only he among Class 3-E makes the top fifty in the first test, but overconfidence costs him against Gakushu Asano at the end of term, and Koro-sensei calls him out for it.
When the class infiltrates a hotel to get an antidote for their poisoned classmates, Karma takes on the hired killer Grip and turns the man's own paralysis gas against him.
Having actually studied over summer, he takes second place overall in the midterms, then beats Gakushu on the final exam's hardest maths question by spotting a simpler approach.
When Nagisa wants to save Koro-sensei, Karma leads the opposing side in a paint-gun battle. Their final duel ends with Nagisa choking him into surrender, and the two become closer friends.

On the deadline night the class holds their teacher down together, and Karma is the first to answer Koro-sensei's last roll call. Seven years later he has passed his government service exams and is starting work at a ministry.

lessons.lesson: Talent without effort gets caught out.
lessons.why: Karma loses to Asano when he coasts, and wins when he actually prepares. Koro-sensei's lesson about pride stays with him.

lessons.lesson: Trust is rebuilt by people who keep showing up.
lessons.why: Koro-sensei earns Karma's respect simply by catching him when he jumps off the cliff.

lessons.lesson: A real fight can save a friendship.
lessons.why: Karma and Nagisa had drifted apart; their all-out duel lets them speak honestly and makes them closer.

relationships.name: Nagisa Shiota
relationships.detail: His friend since first year, whose hidden talent for assassination Karma recognises; their duel decides the class's split.

relationships.name: Koro-sensei
relationships.detail: The tentacled teacher Karma first sets out to humiliate, and the first adult since his betrayal whom he really trusts.

relationships.name: Gakushu Asano
relationships.detail: The chairman's son and the school's top student, whom Karma loses to and later beats.

relationships.name: Kaede Kayano
relationships.detail: Karma teases her about her feelings for Nagisa and is part of the class that fights alongside her.

relationships.name: Tadaomi Karasuma
relationships.detail: The Ministry of Defence agent who drills Class 3-E in combat and assassination skills.

relationships.name: Ryoma Terasaka
relationships.detail: The class bruiser, whose straightforward nature makes him a favourite target of Karma's pranks; Terasaka eventually comes to respect him.

strength.rank: Class 3-E's most dangerous student
strength.summary: Karma combines years of street fighting with a quick tactical mind. He is the first student to land a hit on Koro-sensei, sneaking anti-sensei knife shards into a handshake, and he dodges, bluffs and improvises against opponents far stronger than him.

fights.title: The handshake
fights.summary: Karma greets Koro-sensei with a handshake laced with knife fragments, the first wound any student lands on him.

fights.title: The cliff jump
fights.summary: He leaps off a cliff gun in hand to force Koro-sensei to choose between saving him and protecting himself; a web of tentacles catches him.

fights.title: Karma vs. Grip
fights.summary: The assassin hits him with paralysis gas, but Karma has covered his mouth and gasses Grip in return so the class can tie him up.

fights.title: Duel with Nagisa
fights.summary: Both lose their knives; Karma bites his tongue to resist Nagisa's clap stunner, but ends up caught in a triangle choke and concedes.

fights.title: Final exam showdown with Asano
fights.summary: Facing the last maths question, Karma finds the elegant solution that Asano misses.

keyEpisodes.why: His arrival and turning point with Koro-sensei.
Koro-sensei scolds him for losing to Gakushu through overconfidence.
The class splits and Karma leads the side determined to finish the job.
His fight with Nagisa and their shared past.
The class says goodbye to Koro-sensei.

qualities.detail: She haggles over everything, keeps the crew's finances on a tight leash and once ran off with the Going Merry and the crew's treasure.
She can feel a storm coming before the instruments do, and her navigation is what gets the Straw Hats through seas other crews avoid.
In Orange Town she uses Luffy as a decoy, pretending he is her boss, so she can slip away from Buggy's crew with their map.
She keeps the men of the crew in line with her fists, especially when Luffy or Usopp does something reckless.
For years she carries her village's debt to Arlong alone so that nobody else there has to pay the price.

nami.backstory: Nami was a war orphan found as a baby by a little girl, Nojiko, and by Bell-mère, a Marine who had just survived a battle. Bell-mère took both girls home to Cocoyashi Village and raised them on a tangerine grove with very little money. Nami showed a gift for maps and navigation from a young age. When Arlong's fish-man pirates seized the village, they demanded a tribute for every person; Bell-mère had only enough to pay for her daughters, and Arlong killed her. Noticing a chart Nami had drawn, Arlong took her into his crew as his mapmaker and offered a deal: raise a hundred million berries and he would sell the village back. For eight years Nami stole from pirates to buy that freedom, hiding the truth from the villagers, who quietly knew all along.

journey.summary: Running from Buggy's crew with a stolen Grand Line map, she literally runs into Luffy. She teams up with him for profit, steals back Buggy's scattered body parts in the final fight and sails on, insisting she is not a pirate.

She steals the Going Merry and returns to Arlong, apparently loyal to him. When Marines in Arlong's pay seize her savings, she slashes in despair at the Arlong tattoo on her arm, then finally asks Luffy for help. He places his straw hat on her and the crew storms Arlong Park.
She guides the ship through the Grand Line, falls dangerously ill on the way to Drum Island, and in Alubarna defeats Miss Doublefinger with the Clima-Tact Usopp built for her.
During the rescue of Robin, she takes on the CP9 agent Kalifa, discovers her soap powers wash away with water, and wins with mirages and lightning, earning her first bounty.

Separated from the crew for two years, she studies the weather science of the sky island Weatheria. In Wano she gains the thundercloud Zeus as an ally and knocks out Ulti of the Tobi Roppo to protect Tama.
The story continues in the manga and anime as of November 2026, with Nami still the crew's navigator and her dream of mapping the whole world unfinished.

lessons.lesson: Asking for help takes more courage than going it alone.
lessons.why: Nami carried Cocoyashi's fate for eight years by herself. Her turning point is finally saying the words to Luffy.

lessons.lesson: Brains can be a weapon.
lessons.why: Against Miss Doublefinger and Kalifa she wins by understanding the weather and her enemy's weaknesses, not by brute strength.

lessons.lesson: A selfish-looking goal can hide a selfless one.
lessons.why: Everyone thinks Nami just loves money. Every berry was really meant to buy back her village.

qualities.detail: He has 'GO! GO! ZEPPELI' worked into his teeth and treats the race like a stage, even ruining the organiser's victory party with exploding wine bottles after being penalised.
He loves bad puns and absurd gags and keeps telling them to Johnny, whether or not anyone laughs.
Raised to be an executioner, he crosses an ocean to save a boy he was ordered to kill.
Toward people who threaten the race or his partner, he is quick and cold, as he shows with the assassin Pork Pie Hat Kid.
He agrees to teach Johnny the Spin only on condition that Gyro stays ahead in the race, then ends up guiding him at every turn.

gyro-zeppeli.backstory: Gyro was born into the Zeppeli family of the Kingdom of Naples, respected doctors who were also, secretly, the king's executioners. His father Gregorio taught him the Spin, a technique that sends a powerful rotation through a pair of steel balls, and at thirteen Gyro learned that it was used to calm prisoners before execution. He trained as both surgeon and executioner and was expected to take over from his father. Then a ten-year-old servant boy named Marco was sentenced to death for a plot against the king he had nothing to do with. Refusing to execute a blameless child, Gyro heard from a royal servant that the king might pardon Marco if Gyro won the Steel Ball Run, a horse race across America with a fifty-million-dollar prize, and he left for San Diego against his father's wishes.

journey.summary: In San Diego he flattens a thief with a spinning steel ball, and a paralysed former jockey, Johnny Joestar, briefly stands after touching it. Gyro crosses the first stage's finish line ahead of everyone, using the Spin to catch the wind.

Penalised for using his steel balls, he grudgingly lets Johnny tag along to learn the Spin. In the desert they beat the insect-controlling Mrs. Robinson and survive the magnetic Boomboom family with Mountain Tim's help.

A terrorist from Naples, Oyecomova, tries to blow him apart; Gyro and Johnny kill him. Healing at the 'Zombie Horse' mural, Gyro reveals his family's secret and the mission to save Marco, then beats the cyborg racer Fritz von Stroheim.

Johnny absorbs a mummified arm, revealing the race as a hunt for a holy corpse organised by President Funny Valentine. Gyro is captured by the assassin Pork Pie Hat Kid, then kills him using the Spin on the arm's nails. The anime was mid-season as of November 2026.

Gyro and Johnny fight more of Valentine's agents, including the fellow Spin user Wekapipo, and Gyro gains the right eye of the corpse. In the final battle he reaches the Golden Spin and his Stand, Ball Breaker, but Valentine's D4C Love Train lets the President outlast him, and Gyro dies of his wounds after passing a final lesson to Johnny.

lessons.lesson: Duty and conscience can pull in opposite directions.
lessons.why: Gyro's family trained him to execute without feeling; saving Marco means defying his father and his king's court.

lessons.lesson: Teaching changes the teacher.
lessons.why: He agrees to train Johnny for selfish reasons, but by the end of the race the student carries Gyro's last lesson into the fight.

lessons.lesson: Swagger can be armour.
lessons.why: Behind the jokes and gold teeth is a man carrying a child's life on his shoulders.

strength.rank: Master of the Spin
strength.summary: Gyro's steel balls carry a rotation that can shatter bones, disrupt muscles or, used as medicine, repair them. He is also a trained surgeon and an expert rider; on the first day he knocks out a thief with a single throw and uses the Spin's airflow to edge ahead in a photo-finish.

fights.title: The thief at the sign-up
fights.summary: He duels a thief at the registration grounds and drops him with a steel ball charged with the Spin.

fights.title: Gyro vs. Mrs. Robinson
fights.summary: Showered with cactus needles in the desert, Gyro's deflected Spin scrambles the insects his pursuer was using against them.

fights.title: Gyro vs. Oyecomova
fights.summary: He steers a bomb blast into his own leg to save his hands, then chases the Neapolitan terrorist across a river with Johnny.

fights.title: Gyro vs. Fritz von Stroheim
fights.summary: Freshly healed, he beats the German cyborg racer with his steel balls.

fights.title: Gyro vs. Pork Pie Hat Kid
fights.summary: Captured as bait, he turns the tables by spinning the corpse arm's fingernails into the assassin.
